a1.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James describes its value proposition as having "the largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody," with critical mass and decades of experience in all of them, and says the value proposition, cultural fit, platform and multiple affiliation options appeal to advisors coming from wires, regionals and other independents.
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody, and we have critical mass and decades of experience in all of them... the value proposition, the cultural fit, the platform that I talked about, the multiple affiliation options, it's appealing to advisors from a lot of different firms.

items.text: The firm describes its "best-of-both-worlds" value proposition as an advisor- and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, and says its strong balance sheet and commitment to independence is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.
items.quote: Our best-of-both-worlds value proposition, where we offer a unique combination of an advisor and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, continues to resonate with advisors... our strong balance sheet and commitment to independence is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.

items.text: The firm cites a 97% advisor satisfaction rate, the largest addressable market in the industry because it offers all the affiliation options an advisor could want, being agnostic about how advisors affiliate, and treating advisors like clients as an increasingly unique combination.
items.quote: we have 97% adviser satisfaction rate... we have the largest addressable market in the industry because we have all the affiliation options that an adviser could possibly want... there's very few firms in the industry that treat advisers like clients anymore.

items.text: The firm says advisors "do not have to choose between culture and capabilities," offering a client-focused culture with leading technologies and products, combined with a strong balance sheet, long-term thinking and commitment to independence that sets it apart.
items.quote: advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities. We offer a unique combination of an adviser and client-focused culture together with leading technologies, products and solutions... Combined with our strong balance sheet, long-term thinking and commitment to independence, that continues to set Raymond James apart

items.text: The firm says it attracts and retains advisors with its unique culture, leading service, and robust platform, whereas competitors compete with the largest check; it values independence to enable objective advice, whereas competitors change comp plans every year to cross-sell bank products.
items.quote: We attract and retain financial advisors with our unique culture, leading service, and robust platform, whereas many of our competitors compete with the largest check. We value independence... whereas many of our competitors change their comp plans every year to cross-sell more bank products.

items.text: The firm says prospective advisors look at its balance sheet and its commitment to remaining independent, and it differentiates on long-term focus, the "Power of Personal" personal relationships, and a roughly $1 billion annual technology investment.
items.quote: they want a platform and a home that can remain independent. And we're absolutely committed to remaining independent... we're focused on the long term, we're focused on the Power of Personal... and we're able to invest $1 billion in technology.

items.text: Shoukry says the firm has "the largest total addressable market based on having all of the affiliation options at scale," so when advisors consider a move they need only assess cultural and capability fit, not whether Raymond James offers a given channel.
items.quote: We have the largest total addressable market based on having all of the affiliation options at scale, and when advisors are thinking about making a move, they don't have to select.

items.text: The firm attributes its recruiting momentum to treating advisors like clients, respecting the relationship advisors have with their clients, and its "best of both worlds" value proposition.
items.quote: the consistency of putting advisors, treating them like clients, and respecting the relationship advisors have with their clients and that best of both worlds value proposition

items.text: The firm describes its "Powerfully Personal" value proposition as increasingly differentiating, doubling down on personal relationships with financial advisors and giving them tools to strengthen their client relationships.
items.quote: The powerfully personal, the value proposition that we released with our annual report... is really doubling and tripling down on what we've always done, which is really focusing on the personal relationships with financial advisors

items.text: The firm's AdvisorChoice platform lets advisors match their professional goals to the affiliation option that is right for them, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility backed by a leading independent financial firm.
items.quote: Through AdvisorChoice®, you have the ability to match your professional goals to the affiliation option that's right for you, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility – and all backed by the full support of a leading independent financial firm.

a1.RJF.reason: The passages contain the firm's own statements describing its value proposition and positioning to recruit advisors, including from wirehouses.

a2.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James brought on breakaway teams from Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley whose combined client assets exceeded $1 billion earlier in 2026.
items.quote: Earlier this year, the firm brought on breakaway teams from Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley whose combined assets exceeded $1 billion

items.text: A team that previously managed more than $550 million in client assets at UBS Financial Services joined Raymond James (The Woodlands, Texas).

a2.RJF.reason: Trade-press passages state specific wirehouse (Wells Fargo, Morgan Stanley, UBS) recruits with asset figures; the firm's own aggregate recruiting production/assets figures are not broken out by wirehouse versus other prior firms.

a3.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James reported that in fiscal year 2025, adjusted compensation expense included the amortization of transition assistance provided to recruited advisors and other retention awards to existing advisors in the aggregate amount of $355 million, an increase of approximately 11% compared to fiscal 2024.
items.quote: In fiscal year 2025, adjusted compensation expense included the amortization of transition assistance provided to recruited advisors and other retention awards to existing advisors in the aggregate amount of $355 million, representing an increase of approximately 11% compared to fiscal 2024.

items.text: Raymond James offers loans to prospective financial advisors for recruiting and retention purposes, and had unfunded commitments of $14 million for loans to financial advisors who had met such conditions as of June 30, 2026.
items.quote: We offer loans to prospective financial advisors for recruiting and retention purposes. ... We had unfunded commitments of $ 14 million for loans to financial advisors who have met such conditions as of June 30, 2026.

items.text: Raymond James has designed a compensation structure and benefit plans intended to be attractive to current and prospective associates, with competitive pay packages including base salary, incentive bonus, and equity compensation, plus annual ESOP and profit-sharing contributions, 401(k) matching, an employee stock purchase plan, and equity awards and non-qualified deferred compensation plans.
items.quote: We have designed a compensation structure, including an array of benefit plans and programs, that is intended to be attractive to current and prospective associates... Our competitive pay packages include base salary, incentive bonus, and equity compensation programs.

items.text: Raymond James states it does not lead with the highest check but offers competitive economics, leading with culture and capabilities, and remaining disciplined on transition assistance and economics to advisers.
items.quote: we don't lead with the highest check. We want to have competitive economics... but we lead with culture and capabilities... We remain disciplined... on those transaction assistance -- transition assistance and economics to advisers.

items.text: Raymond James prefers to recruit advisors one by one where they are a good cultural fit, with 100% of transition assistance paid going to retention rather than to a seller.
items.quote: we'd much rather recruit one by one, where we know the advisors are a good cultural fit, and 100% of what we pay in transition assistance is going to retention versus the seller.

items.text: Raymond James positions its 'best of both worlds' value proposition, combining an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology, products, and services, as what resonates with advisors.
items.quote: our best of both worlds value proposition, where we have the culture, the advisor and client-focused culture... and coupling that with the resources and the platform and the technology and the products and services that we offer

items.text: Raymond James positions the 'Power of Personal' value proposition, focusing on personal relationships with financial advisors and giving them tools and resources to strengthen client relationships.
items.quote: really focusing on the personal relationships with financial advisors and giving them tools and resources to strengthen the personal relationships that they have with their clients.

items.text: Raymond James positions its strong balance sheet, long-term focus, and commitment to independence as setting it apart for advisors evaluating alternatives.
items.quote: Together with our strong balance sheet, long-term focus and commitment to independence, that combination continues to set Raymond James apart for advisers evaluating alternatives.

items.text: Raymond James offers affiliation options with payout percentages of up to 50% for Traditional Employee, 70-80% for Advisor Select, and 81% to 90% for Independent Contractor and Corporate RIA, plus employee benefits offerings.
items.quote: Model: Traditional Employee ... Up to 50% payout** and full array of competitive employee benefits offerings. ... Model: Advisor Select ... 70-80% gross payout** ... Model: Independent Contractor ... 81% to 90% payout***

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended December 31, 2025, the firm described its value proposition as having the largest addressable market across its affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to RIA custody, with critical mass and decades of experience in all of them, and said the value proposition, cultural fit, platform, and multiple affiliation options appeal to advisors coming from wires, regionals, and other independents.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended September 30, 2025, the firm described its best-of-both-worlds value proposition as an advisor- and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, and said its strong balance sheet and commitment to independence is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended June 30, 2026, the firm cited a 97% advisor satisfaction rate, the largest addressable market in the industry because it offers all the affiliation options an advisor could want, being agnostic about how advisors affiliate, and treating advisors like clients as an increasingly unique combination.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended March 31, 2026, the firm said advisors do not have to choose between culture and capabilities, offering a client-focused culture with leading technologies and products, combined with a strong balance sheet, long-term thinking, and commitment to independence that sets it apart.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended September 30, 2025, the firm said it attracts and retains advisors with its unique culture, leading service, and robust platform, whereas many competitors compete with the largest check; it values independence to enable objective advice, whereas many competitors change their comp plans every year to cross-sell bank products.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended December 31, 2025, the firm said prospective advisors look at its balance sheet and its commitment to remaining independent, and it differentiates on long-term focus, the Power of Personal relationships, and a roughly $1 billion annual technology investment.

Raymond James Financial: In a trade-press report published October 29, 2026, CEO Paul Shoukry said the firm has the largest total addressable market based on having all of the affiliation options at scale, so when advisors consider a move they need only assess cultural and capability fit, not whether Raymond James offers a given channel.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended March 31, 2025, the firm attributed its recruiting momentum to treating advisors like clients, respecting the relationship advisors have with their clients, and its best-of-both-worlds value proposition.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended December 31, 2025, the firm described its Powerfully Personal value proposition as increasingly differentiating, doubling down on personal relationships with financial advisors and giving them tools to strengthen their client relationships.

Raymond James Financial: The firm's AdvisorChoice platform (company web page, page content as of April 21, 2026) lets advisors match their professional goals to the affiliation option that is right for them, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom, and flexibility backed by a leading independent financial firm.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: Trade press reported (published November 5, 2026) that earlier in 2026 the firm brought on breakaway teams from Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley whose combined client assets exceeded $1 billion.

Raymond James Financial: Trade press reported (published September 2, 2026) that a team that previously managed more than $550 million in client assets at UBS Financial Services joined Raymond James in The Woodlands, Texas.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended September 30, 2025, the firm reported that in fiscal year 2025, adjusted compensation expense included the amortization of transition assistance provided to recruited advisors and other retention awards to existing advisors in the aggregate amount of $355 million, an increase of approximately 11% compared to fiscal 2024.

Raymond James Financial: The 10-Q for the period ended June 30, 2026 states the firm offers loans to prospective financial advisors for recruiting and retention purposes, and had unfunded commitments of $14 million for loans to financial advisors who had met such conditions as of June 30, 2026.

Raymond James Financial: The 10-K for the period ended September 30, 2025 states the firm has designed a compensation structure and benefit plans intended to be attractive to current and prospective associates, with competitive pay packages including base salary, incentive bonus, and equity compensation, plus annual ESOP and profit-sharing contributions, 401(k) matching, an employee stock purchase plan, and equity awards and non-qualified deferred compensation plans.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended June 30, 2026, the firm stated it does not lead with the highest check but offers competitive economics, leading with culture and capabilities, and remaining disciplined on transition assistance and economics to advisors.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended December 31, 2025, the firm said it prefers to recruit advisors one by one where they are a good cultural fit, with 100% of transition assistance paid going to retention rather than to a seller.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended September 30, 2025, the firm positioned its best-of-both-worlds value proposition, combining an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology, products, and services, as what resonates with advisors.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended December 31, 2025, the firm positioned the Power of Personal value proposition, focusing on personal relationships with financial advisors and giving them tools and resources to strengthen client relationships.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended June 30, 2026, the firm positioned its strong balance sheet, long-term focus, and commitment to independence as setting it apart for advisors evaluating alternatives.

Raymond James Financial: The firm's recruiting page (page content as of April 21, 2026) states affiliation options with payout percentages of up to 50% for Traditional Employee, 70-80% for Advisor Select, and 81% to 90% for Independent Contractor and Corporate RIA, plus employee benefits offerings.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: As of September 30, 2025, the firm had 8,943 total financial advisors, comprising 3,878 employee financial advisors and 5,065 independent contractor advisors; advisors in the firm's RCS division are not included in this financial advisor metric although their client assets are included in PCG AUA.
Raymond James Financial: As of September 30, 2024, the firm had 8,787 total financial advisors, comprising 3,826 employee financial advisors and 4,961 independent contractor advisors.
Raymond James Financial: As of September 30, 2023, the firm had 8,712 total financial advisors, comprising 3,693 employee financial advisors and 5,019 independent contractor advisors.

Raymond James Financial: The 10-K states the number of financial advisors increased as of September 30, 2025 compared to the prior year, as new recruits and trainees that moved into production roles exceeded departures and planned retirements.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended September 30, 2025, the firm said it ended fiscal year 2025 with a record number of financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year, reflecting solid advisor retention as well as strong recruiting results.

Raymond James Financial: Trade press reported (published November 4, 2026) that an Ohio hire extends a consistent run of Raymond James & Associates recruiting from UBS throughout 2026, as wirehouse advisors respond to changes in how the firm compensates its advisor workforce. Why it might matter: the source states that at Raymond James, advisors gain the freedom, resources, and dedicated support to shape their practice around their clients' evolving needs while continuing to grow on their own terms.

Raymond James Financial: In a press release for the period ended June 30, 2026, CEO Paul Shoukry stated the firm enters the fiscal fourth quarter with significant momentum supported by robust financial advisor recruiting. Why it might matter: the source states this momentum is supported by historically strong business drivers, including fee-based assets reaching a quarter-end record of $1.15 trillion and annualized domestic Private Client Group net new asset growth of 6.6% for the first nine months of the fiscal year.

Raymond James Financial: In a press release for the period ended March 31, 2026, CEO Paul Shoukry stated that financial advisor recruiting activity across all the firm's affiliation options remains robust. Why it might matter: the source states the firm is investing in industry-leading technology solutions, including increasing AI integration, to improve efficiency and provide financial professionals more time to serve their clients.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended March 31, 2026, CEO Paul Shoukry said confidence in recruiting is driven by the volume of home office visits with prospective advisors and new commits, with an uptick of commits in the employee affiliation option. Why it might matter: the source notes there seem to be catalysts for advisor movement every 12 to 18 months over the 16 years he has been with the firm.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended December 31, 2025, CEO Paul Shoukry attributed solid recruiting momentum and net new asset annualized growth of 8% this quarter to the firm's appeal to financial advisors. Why it might matter: the source attributes this to the strength and consistency of the firm's client-first culture, a robust technology and products platform, and its strong balance sheet.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended December 31, 2025, CEO Paul Shoukry stated financial advisor recruiting activity remains strong. Why it might matter: the source states the firm entered the second fiscal quarter with record client assets and strong competitive positioning across all of its businesses.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended December 31, 2025, CEO Paul Shoukry stated the firm recruited financial advisors to its domestic independent contractor and employee channels in the fiscal first quarter with trailing twelve-month production totaling $96 million and approximately $13 billion of client assets at their previous firms. Why it might matter: the source describes this as a strong result for a quarter that typically experiences a seasonal slowdown.

Raymond James Financial: A comparison to the firm's own prior periods can be made on this evidence. Trade press reported trailing 12-month production of $538 million for recruited advisors coming into the firm's domestic independent contractor and employee channels during fiscal 2026, up from $407 million in the prior fiscal year; the firm separately reported recruiting production advisors with prior production of over $400 million in fiscal 2025 (up 21% over the prior year's record) and approximately $335 million of trailing 12-month production in fiscal 2024. A comparison to competitors cannot be made on this evidence: the only competitor references supplied are the firm's own self-assessments, such as a 97% advisor satisfaction rate the CEO describes as the best he knows of in the industry and 7% annualized net new assets for the first half of its fiscal year that it describes as leading the industry, with no competitor figures provided to verify them.

a1.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: CEO Rick Wurster states Schwab has built its adviser business around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed.
items.quote: We have built our adviser business around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed.

items.text: Schwab states it maintains its competitive position through sales, support, technology and business consulting teams dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed in serving their clients.
items.quote: Management believes that we can maintain our competitive position primarily through the efforts of our sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams, which are dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed in serving their clients.

items.text: Schwab states that, in addition to focusing on superior service, it utilizes technology to provide RIAs with a highly-developed, scalable platform for administering their clients' assets easily and efficiently.
items.quote: In addition to focusing on superior service, we utilize technology to provide RIAs with a highly-developed, scalable platform for administering their clients' assets easily and efficiently.

items.text: CEO Rick Wurster states Schwab is deepening relationships with the RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs.
items.quote: In our advisor services business, we're deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms we serve by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs.

items.text: CEO Rick Wurster states Schwab will continue to focus on its custody services for RIAs with under $100 million AUM, and that its role is to provide a platform and support ecosystem that helps advisors serve clients and helps their firms thrive.
items.quote: Our job and our role is to provide a platform and a support ecosystem that helps you support your clients and helps your firm thrive.

items.text: CEO Rick Wurster states Schwab wants to give RIAs equal or better access than their wirehouse counterparts to banking services such as lending, private market investing, and long-short investment strategies.
items.quote: Schwab wants to give registered investment advisors equal or better access than their wirehouse counterparts to banking services such as lending , private market investing, and long-short investment strategies, CEO Rick Wurster said

items.text: CEO Rick Wurster states Schwab continues to invest in Advisor Services, making it easier for advisers to do business with Schwab and rounding out its offering by adding more lending capabilities.
items.quote: we continue to invest in this business, make it easier for advisers to do business with us. We've rounded out our offering to them in terms of adding more lending capabilities

items.text: CEO Rick Wurster states that in advisor services, Schwab is adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while helping new advisors transition to independence.
items.quote: In advisor services, we are adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence.

items.text: CEO Rick Wurster states Schwab has tried to make the path to independence as easy as possible for advisors, investing in its own process and working with partners to provide a ready experience and an easy transition.
items.quote: We've tried to make the path to independence as easy as possible," Wurster said. "We've invested in our own process. We work with partners like we did with Open Arc. We work with Dynasty … collectively, we try to have a great experience ready for them, and try to make the transition easy once they decide they want to be independent.

items.text: CEO Rick Wurster states Schwab is increasingly trying to play the role of being the RIA's bank and helping them manage both sides of the balance sheet for their clients.
items.quote: We are increasingly trying to play a role of being their bank and helping them manage both sides of the balance sheet for their clients.

a1.SCHW.reason: The passages contain multiple explicit statements by Schwab management describing its strategy for the RIA custody business (helping RIAs grow/compete/succeed, providing a support ecosystem beyond custody, banking/lending capabilities, technology platform, and supporting transition to independence), so these are facts.

a2.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab states it is adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence.
items.quote: In advisor services, we are adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence.

items.text: Schwab states it has built its adviser business around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed, and that it is continuing to invest in the business to meet advisers' needs.
items.quote: We have built our adviser business around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed... We are continuing to invest in this business to meet advisers' needs.

items.text: Schwab states it is deepening relationships with the RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs.
items.quote: we're deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms we serve by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs.

items.text: Schwab states it launched Advisor ProDirect, a fee-based, membership-driven offer designed to support independence for new RIAs.
items.quote: we launched Advisor ProDirect, a fee-based, membership-driven offer designed to support independence for new RIAs.

items.text: Schwab states it will continue to focus on its custody services for RIAs with under $100 million AUM, and that its role is to provide a platform and support ecosystem that helps advisors support clients and their firms thrive.
items.quote: Schwab will continue to focus on its custody services for registered investment advisors with under $100 million AUM... "Our job and our role is to provide a platform and a support ecosystem that helps you support your clients and helps your firm thrive."

items.text: Schwab states it wants to give RIAs equal or better access than wirehouses to banking services such as lending, private market investing, and long-short investment strategies, citing these as focus areas for its custody offerings.
items.quote: Schwab wants to give registered investment advisors equal or better access than their wirehouse counterparts to banking services such as lending, private market investing, and long-short investment strategies... focus areas for its custody offerings.

items.text: Schwab states the opportunity going forward is to offer a more curated set of alternatives to its advisors rather than primarily custodying the assets.
items.quote: I think the opportunity going forward is for us to be -- offer a more curated set of alternatives to our advisors and to be bringing them to those advisor clients as opposed to primarily being in a position of just custodying the assets.

items.text: Schwab states it could do more to curate and help advisers choose the right alternative investments for their clients and to make investing in alternatives easy for advisers.
items.quote: we think we could do more to curate and help advisers along the way choose the right alternative investments for their clients and create a platform that is very helpful to them... make investing in alternative investments easy for our advisers

items.text: Schwab states it maintains its competitive position through sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed, and it utilizes technology to provide RIAs with a scalable platform for administering client assets.
items.quote: Management believes that we can maintain our competitive position primarily through the efforts of our sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams, which are dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed in serving their clients... we utilize technology to provide RIAs with a highly-developed, scalable platform

items.text: A Schwab spokesperson states the firm remains focused on investing in innovation, capabilities, and service to help advisors grow and investors succeed.
items.quote: we remain focused on investing in innovation, capabilities, and service to help advisors grow and investors succeed.

a2.SCHW.reason: Multiple passages state Schwab's priorities for its RIA custody business, including serving RIAs of all sizes, building a support ecosystem beyond custody, banking capabilities, and curated alternatives.

a3.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab's 10-K states that in the Advisor Services arena it competes with institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks, and trust companies.
items.quote: In the Advisor Services arena, we compete with institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks, and trust companies.

items.text: Fidelity Investments is named as the second-largest custodian after Schwab, a competitor in RIA custody.
items.quote: Wurster's comments come after Fidelity Investments, the second-largest custodian after Schwab, told RIAs in early October that firms with under $100 million in client assets will have to leave the platform by June 30, 2027.

items.text: Fidelity Investments is named, along with Schwab, as a legacy custodian with a commanding lead over Altruist.
items.quote: The legacy custodians, Schwab and Fidelity Investments, still have a commanding lead over Altruist in the marketplace, but Vanguard's backing, along with its own advice business, makes it a more formidable competitor.

items.text: Vanguard, through its acquisition of Altruist, is described as a competitor that 'raises the stakes' for legacy custodians Schwab and Fidelity in the RIA custody business.
items.quote: Vanguard and Altruist shifted the custodial playing field overnight with the global asset managers $4.6 billion outlay for the scrappy, tech-focused custody platform... For Schwab and Fidelity, this raises the stakes without necessarily shifting the landscape overnight.

items.text: Vanguard is described as being set up to compete with Fidelity and Schwab in RIA custody.
items.quote: Now, Vanguard is saying we are an RIA custodian, and we're a technology platform provider... this clearly sets them up to compete with Fidelity for sure, and arguably it sets them up competitively with Schwab.

items.text: SEI, Goldman Sachs, and Robinhood are named as other custodians that RIAs might look to as alternatives to Schwab.
items.quote: Do they start looking at SEI ? Do they start looking at Goldman? Do they start looking at the lead flow through Robinhood ?

items.text: Fidelity is named as Schwab's close rival, and Altruist (Vanguard-owned) is named as another custodian.
items.quote: Schwab's close rival, Fidelity , offers up to 1.94% on sweep cash, and 3.49% through its money market funds. The now Vanguard-owned custodian, Altruist, offers 0.05% in sweep accounts, and a maximum 3.75% through a high-yield cash account.

a3.SCHW.reason: Multiple passages name specific competitors (Fidelity, Vanguard, Altruist, SEI, Goldman, Robinhood) and categories of competitors in the RIA custody business.

a5.SCHW.label: different_quantity

items.text: Schwab states it serves more than 16,000 RIA firms on its custody platform, a count of firms rather than a headcount of advisors.
items.quote: we serve more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets with a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities

items.text: Schwab noted it has some 3,000 financial advisors in-house, which are Schwab's own retail advisors rather than advisors at independent RIA firms custodying with Schwab.
items.quote: Schwab noted that it has some 3,000 financial advisors in-house, many of whom hold CFPs.

a5.SCHW.differs_because: No passage states an advisor headcount for the RIA custody business. The passages report a count of RIA firms (16,000) and Schwab's own in-house financial advisors (3,000), not the number of advisors at independent RIAs custodying with Schwab.
a5.SCHW.reason: The asked quantity (advisor headcount for the RIA custody business) is not stated; the passages give related but different quantities (firm count and in-house advisors).

a6.SCHW.label: fact

items.quote: we announced a strategic investment in wealth.com... this investment is one part of our broader effort to provide more of an ecosystem for our RIA clients as we help them grow, compete, and succeed

The Charles Schwab Corporation: On the 1Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), Schwab stated it recently launched a structured asset lending program for advisers, which lets advisers' clients borrow against alternative investments, restricted shares, and private shares rather than introducing a big bank. Why it might matter: historically advisers had to introduce a big bank to do that lending, and now they can keep the wealth relationship with Schwab.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: On the 1Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), Schwab stated it believes it could do more to curate and help advisers choose the right alternative investments and create a helpful platform, and sees opportunities to monetize the provision of alternatives to advisers; it has leaned into making investing in alternatives easy for advisers. Why it might matter: Schwab said it believes there will be opportunities to monetize the provision of those alternatives to its advisers as that develops.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), Schwab stated that in Advisor Services it is expanding its wealth services offer (including the Model Market Center platform and alternative investments), expanding lending and trust services to advisors through Charles Schwab Bank, and launching a high-touch trading service for block trades in Q1. Why it might matter: the wealth services offer is designed to simplify processes and help advisors compete and serve their clients' comprehensive needs.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Schwab stated it is deepening relationships with its RIA firms by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone, having grown lending support and alternatives capability, expanded its institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform to nearly 60 managers, and launched Advisor ProDirect for breakaway advisors. Why it might matter: Schwab described driving growth by deepening relationships with its clients as its first focus area.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Schwab stated it supported the largest advisor transition in the history of the industry by welcoming OpenArc to its platform in September. Why it might matter: it advances Schwab's stated effort to add support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while helping new advisors transition to independence.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: On the 1Q25 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2025), Schwab stated it announced a strategic investment in wealth.com, a leader in digital estate planning, which it describes as one part of its broader effort to provide more of an ecosystem for its RIA clients to help them grow, compete, and succeed. Why it might matter: the investment enhances Schwab's estate planning capabilities and experience for clients as part of meeting their needs.

a1.MER.label: fact

items.text: Merrill's CFO stated that the firm is picking up recruiting of experienced advisors, but that this is not an enormous part of its strategy; the strategy is a training program to train people in wealth management at Bank of America and Merrill.
items.quote: we're picking up the recruiting of experienced advisors. That isn't an enormous part of our strategy, but it's a training program so that we're training people in wealth management, Bank of America, and Merrill

items.text: Merrill continued to add financial advisors to the sales force through its extensive training program and through experienced hiring of advisors.
items.quote: We also continued to add financial advisors to the sales force in Merrill and the Private Bank through our extensive training program and experienced hiring of advisors.

items.text: Merrill executives touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm returned to veteran broker recruiting; the firm had largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 but returned after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer in 2023.
items.quote: Merrill executives in October touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm has returned to veteran broker recruiting. The firm largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 but returned after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf, who took over in 2023, restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer.

items.text: Merrill's CFO said the leadership's focus is to keep growing the sales force, and that advisor attrition is now at near historic lows.
items.quote: So I think what Lindsay and Eric are trying to drive there, what Katy is trying to drive there is just keep growing the sales force. Well, adviser attrition is now at near historic lows.

items.text: Merrill is driving productivity higher on both newer and existing financial advisors and continues to attract talent across both new and experienced advisors.
items.quote: We're driving productivity higher on both newer and existing members of our financial advisers team, and we continue to attract talent across both new and experienced advisers.

items.text: Merrill operates an Advisor Development Program (ADP) with roles including ADP Client Associate, ADP Financial Solutions Advisor, ADP Financial Advisor, and Merrill Core Advisor, through which participants progress until graduating to Merrill Core Advisor.
items.quote: After mastering key objectives and pre-determined targets, progress through three roles until you graduate to Merrill Core Advisor.

items.text: Merrill continued to attract talented advisors who are drawn to the breadth of its platform and its ability to deliver comprehensive solutions for clients.
items.quote: both Merrill and the Private Bank continued to attract talented advisers who are drawn to the breadth of our platform and our ability to deliver comprehensive solutions for clients.

a1.MER.reason: The passages directly describe Merrill's advisor growth strategy: a training program (Advisor Development Program) plus recruiting of experienced/veteran advisors, growing the sales force, and driving advisor productivity.

a2.MER.label: fact

items.text: According to CFO Alastair Borthwick, Merrill's advisor growth strategy is primarily a training program—training people in wealth management at Bank of America and Merrill—rather than recruiting experienced advisors, which he said is "not an enormous part of our strategy."
items.quote: we're picking up the recruiting of experienced advisors. That isn't an enormous part of our strategy, but it's a training program so that we're training people in wealth management, Bank of America, and Merrill, and that's ultimately what we believe we can just keep driving in order to improve the net new flows.

items.text: Borthwick said Merrill leadership is focused on "just keep growing the sales force," noting advisor attrition is now at near historic lows, and that they intend to keep growing over the next 3 to 5 years.
items.quote: So I think what Lindsay and Eric are trying to drive there, what Katy is trying to drive there is just keep growing the sales force. Well, adviser attrition is now at near historic lows.

items.text: Borthwick said Merrill remains focused on pricing discipline, advisor productivity and long-term client relationships, driving productivity higher across both newer and existing financial advisors while continuing to attract talent across both new and experienced advisors.
items.quote: We remain focused on pricing discipline, adviser productivity and long-term client relationships. We're driving productivity higher on both newer and existing members of our financial advisers team, and we continue to attract talent across both new and experienced advisers.

items.text: Borthwick said Merrill and the Private Bank continued to add financial advisors to the sales force through the firm's "extensive training program and experienced hiring of advisors," and that approximately one-third of net new households in Q2 were added by newly trained advisors.
items.quote: We also continued to add financial advisors to the sales force in Merrill and the Private Bank through our extensive training program and experienced hiring of advisors. Approximately one-third of net new households in Q2 were added by our newly trained advisors.

items.text: Borthwick said Merrill's results reflect the firm's "ability to attract clients and experienced advisers to the platform."
items.quote: These results reflect strong demand for advice, and our ability to attract clients and experienced advisers to the platform.

items.text: Merrill's stated foundational belief (investor day) is that "having the best advisors enables us to deliver exceptional client outcomes."
items.quote: …having the best advisors enables us to deliver exceptional client outcomes

items.text: Merrill's recruiting page describes its Advisor Development Program, a training program through which advisors progress through roles to become a Merrill Core (Financial) Advisor.
items.quote: If you're interested in a career in wealth management and possess the entrepreneurial spirit - the Advisor Development Program is for you.

items.text: Merrill executives said recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm returned to veteran broker recruiting; the firm largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 but returned after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf took over in 2023 and restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer.
items.quote: Merrill executives in October touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm has returned to veteran broker recruiting. The firm largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 but returned after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf, who took over in 2023, restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer.

a2.MER.reason: Management statements across transcripts, investor day and press describe the advisor growth strategy directly (training program, growing the sales force, attracting new and experienced advisors, and the shift back to veteran recruiting).

items.text: Morgan Stanley management says the firm continues to invest in Wealth, Institutional Securities and Investment Management via human capital and technology, with growth plans embedding the increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and inside its client base.
items.quote: We continue to invest in each of our three business segments: Wealth, Institutional Securities, and Investment Management via human capital and technology. Our growth plans embed the increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and inside our client base.

items.text: Management describes early AI use cases including LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform focused on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with the firm's financial advisors.
items.quote: These include the DevGen AI tool, which enhances developer efficiency by modernizing code, Parable, an interactive tool that quickly analyzes and summarizes data, and LeadIQ, our AI-powered lead distribution platform, focusing on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with our financial advisors.

items.text: Management describes technology priorities for the advisor business as including protecting client assets and resiliency, and notes that world-class technology can help financial advisors by doing a lot of the early work for client decisions.
items.quote: Third, and this is critical, is the ability to protect client assets... if the technology is world-class, folks want to make decisions with their financial advisers based on the complexity and singularity of their own financial needs... that is something that technology can help do a lot of the early work.

items.text: Management describes using technology for both efficiency (cost side) and revenue (including some AI), as part of the investment story in technology, including in the E*TRADE franchise and E*TRADE Pro.
items.quote: We are also using technology to help us from an efficiency perspective, both on the cost and the revenue side. I'd note to you that some of the AI that we've been doing is actually also on the revenue side.

items.text: Management describes that against its platform of self-directed, workplace and advisor-led channels, the firm has built advantages that make technology a differentiator in its favor.
items.quote: And against that platform, we have built a number of advantages that not only allow us to preserve our moat, but actually make technology a differentiator in our favor.

items.text: Management states the firm's scale supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools, positioning it to lead as the future of wealth management takes shape.
items.quote: while our scale supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools. Together, these strengths provide us with a powerful competitive advantage that positions us to lead as the future of wealth management takes shape.

items.quote: So LeadIQ, for example, which is helping us introduce our advisors to our clients who are interested in advice, that's happening using AI. So there's technology that can be used both on the revenue side and on the expense side.

a1.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James states that through AdvisorChoice advisors can match their professional goals to the affiliation option that is right for them, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility, all backed by the full support of a leading independent financial firm.
items.quote: Through AdvisorChoice®, you have the ability to match your professional goals to the affiliation option that's right for you, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility – and all backed by the full support of a leading independent financial firm.

items.text: Raymond James describes AdvisorChoice as 'a platform of dynamic options and the freedom to choose among them.'
items.quote: AdvisorChoice® - A platform of dynamic options and the freedom to choose among them.

items.text: Raymond James lists its affiliation options as Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA, each with a brief description of what it offers.
items.quote: Traditional Employee: Get everything you expect from working for a firm with a powerful difference – book ownership. Advisor Select: Lead your own branch with access to administrative support and full corporate benefits. Independent Contractor: Operate as an independent financial advisor backed by the resources of a national leader. Bank & Credit Union: Leverage national strength and local impact to grow your advisory business. Corporate RIA: Exercise true autonomy and support refined for fee-only practices under our established RIA.

items.text: Raymond James describes its RIA & Custody Services affiliation option as taking strategic, financial and administrative control of a practice with a full-service partner at the ready.
items.quote: RIA & Custody Services: Take strategic, financial and administrative control of your practice with a full-service partner at the ready.

items.text: Raymond James states in its 10-K that it offers multiple affiliation options referred to as AdvisorChoice, and that financial advisors primarily affiliate directly as employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through its RIA and Custody Services division.
items.quote: We offer multiple affiliation options, which we refer to as AdvisorChoice®. Financial advisors primarily affiliate with us directly as either employees or independent contractors or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors (“RIAs”) and broker-dealers to which we provide services through our RIA and Custody Services (“RCS”) division.
items.definition: Financial advisors primarily affiliate with us directly as either employees or independent contractors or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors and broker-dealers to which we provide services through our RIA and Custody Services division.

items.text: Raymond James states that employee financial advisors work in a traditional branch supported by local management and administrative staff, serve predominantly retail clients, receive compensation primarily as a payout on revenues they generate, and participate in the firm's employee benefit plans.
items.quote: Employee financial advisors work in a traditional branch supported by local management and administrative staff. They provide services predominantly to retail clients. Compensation for these financial advisors primarily includes a payout on revenues they generate and such advisors also participate in the firm's employee benefit plans.

items.text: Raymond James states that independent contractor financial advisors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and accordingly receive a higher payout percentage than employee financial advisors, and that they may affiliate directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in its Financial Institutions Division.
items.quote: Our financial advisors who are independent contractors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and, accordingly, receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors.

items.text: Raymond James states that independent contractor financial advisors may affiliate with it directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in its Financial Institutions Division, and with specific approval on a limited basis may conduct certain other approved business activities.
items.quote: Independent contractor financial advisors may affiliate with us directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in our Financial Institutions Division. With specific approval, and on a limited basis, they are permitted to conduct certain other approved business activities, such as offering insurance products, independent registered investment advisory services, and accounting and tax services.

items.text: Raymond James presents its affiliation models as a spectrum under AdvisorChoice spanning Employee Advisor (RJA), Advisor Select, Independent Advisor (ICD), Banks and Credit Unions, IAR (Corporate RIA), and RIA & Custody Services, stating the AdvisorChoice spectrum services the largest addressable market in the industry and that the movement to independence is not channel-specific.
items.quote: EMPLOYEE ADVISOR (RJA) / ADVISOR SELECT / INDEPENDENT ADVISOR (ICD) / BANKS AND CREDIT UNIONS / IAR* (CORPORATE RIA) / RIA** & CUSTODY SERVICES ... The movement to "independence" is not channel-specific

items.text: Raymond James's CEO states the firm has the largest addressable market across its affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to RIA custody, and that it has critical mass and decades of experience in all of them, not a new venture it is testing.
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody, and we have critical mass and decades of experience in all of them. It's not a new venture for us. It's not something that we're testing out or trying out

a1.RJF.reason: The passages contain multiple statements by Raymond James describing and defining its affiliation models (AdvisorChoice and its component options), so I extracted each substantive descriptive statement as a fact item.

a2.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James states it is agnostic to how advisors affiliate, offering advisor choice and the largest addressable market because it has all affiliation options.
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market in the industry because we have all the affiliation options that an adviser could possibly want. And we have adviser choice where we're agnostic into how you affiliate with Raymond James.

items.text: Raymond James states it has the largest addressable market across its affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to RIA custody, with critical mass and decades of experience in all of them.
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody, and we have critical mass and decades of experience in all of them.

items.text: Raymond James describes AdvisorChoice® as giving advisors the ability to match professional goals to the affiliation option that is right for them, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility.
items.quote: Through AdvisorChoice®, you have the ability to match your professional goals to the affiliation option that's right for you, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility – and all backed by the full support of a leading independent financial firm.

items.text: Raymond James states its independent contractor financial advisor options are designed to help advisors build their businesses with as much or as little of its support as they determine they need.
items.quote: Our independent contractor financial advisor options are designed to help our advisors build their businesses with as much or as little of our support as they determine they need.

items.text: Raymond James refers to its multiple affiliation options as AdvisorChoice®.
items.quote: We offer multiple affiliation options, which we refer to as AdvisorChoice®.

items.text: Raymond James states the AdvisorChoice spectrum services the largest addressable market in the industry and that the movement to independence is not channel-specific.
items.quote: The AdvisorChoice spectrum services the largest addressable market in the industry ... The movement to "independence" is not channel-specific

items.text: Raymond James states its commitment to independence, coupled with its value proposition and strong balance sheet, is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.
items.quote: This value proposition, coupled with our strong balance sheet and commitment to independence, is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.

items.text: Raymond James describes a 'best-of-both-worlds' value proposition, combining an advisor and client-focused culture with its platform, technology, products and services.
items.quote: our best-of-both-worlds value proposition, where we have the culture, the advisor and client-focused culture that we have, the values long-term oriented, always putting clients first in everything that we do, and coupling that with the resources and the platform and the technology and the products and services that we offer

a2.RJF.reason: Multiple passages describe Raymond James's priorities and strategy behind its affiliation models (advisor choice, agnosticism, largest addressable market, best-of-both-worlds, support with flexibility).

a3.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James says there is more competition in its space, and that many competitors compete with the largest check, change their comp plans every year to cross-sell more bank products, and increasingly look for an exit in three to five years.
items.quote: While in some ways there's more competition in our space, we are confident that our longstanding approach is becoming increasingly differentiated and unique... many of our competitors compete with the largest check... many of our competitors change their comp plans every year to cross-sell more bank products

items.text: Raymond James says many of its competitors are increasingly looking for an exit in three to five years or even less.
items.quote: whereas so many of our competitors are increasingly looking for an exit in three to five years or even less

items.text: Raymond James identifies private-equity-backed roll-ups as a relatively novel competitive dynamic of the last five years, noting they have been extremely aggressive in paying higher and higher multiples.
items.quote: The dynamic that's relatively novel in the last five years is these PE-backed roll-ups cropping up everywhere. Over the last three years in particular, they've been extremely aggressive in trading and paying at higher and higher multiples.

items.text: Raymond James says roll-ups, in the absence of a value proposition, compete with big checks.
items.quote: We always say with the roll-ups, in the absence of a value proposition, they compete with big checks.

The firm stated (earnings call, period ended March 31, 2026) that over the last year much more of its recruiting has come from the independent side versus the employee side, calling it a mix shift, and that this mix shift concerns the compensation ratio more than margin due to the payout difference between the independent and employee channels; it also said the independent channel's acceleration rate is probably higher, and trade press reported the independent contractor channel is seeing the most interest in dollar volume while RIA custody grows at a high percentage rate on a smaller base. On assets, Domestic PCG assets under administration by channel are reported only at two dates — Employee $332 billion (March 31, 2020) to $631 billion (March 31, 2025), Independent Contractor $318 billion to $543 billion, and RCS $46 billion to $186 billion — while RCS division AUA is reported on a different quarterly basis from June 30, 2024 to September 30, 2025, so the two bases cannot be joined into one series.

a1.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley states employee loans are granted under a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors, are full recourse and generally require periodic repayments, and are due in full upon termination of employment.
items.quote: Employee loans are granted in conjunction with a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors, are full recourse and generally require periodic repayments, and are due in full upon termination of employment with the Firm.

items.text: CFO Sharon Yeshaya says Morgan Stanley has a great platform with strength in all three channels, and that from the advisor-led side the firm does have recruiting, but it also has flows coming in from workplace.
items.quote: There's obviously a great platform. We have recruits that are interested in what we've been investing in... From the advisor-led side, we do have recruiting, but we also have flows coming in from workplace.

items.text: CEO Ted Pick says the firm is selective about recruiting, that the integrated firm offers unique access to intellectual capital, world-class technology and compensation viewed to be fair and motivating, and that the firm is receiving a lot of inbound inquiry from advisors.
items.quote: we can offer unique access to intellectual capital, world-class technology, compensation that is viewed to be fair and motivating, and the entire thing works. What is happening is we are selective about it, but it is fair to say that Jed and Vince are getting a lot of inbound inquiry

items.text: CFO Sharon Yeshaya says advisor-led flows were particularly strong, originating from new advisors who are attracted to the strength of the workplace, as well as assets that originated from workplace.
items.quote: Advisor-led flows were particularly strong, originating from new advisors who are attracted to the strength of the workplace, as well as assets that originated from workplace.

items.text: CFO Sharon Yeshaya says net new assets were supported by broad-based strength across channels, including positive recruiting trends.
items.quote: The result was supported by broad-based strength across channels, inclusive of elevated flows related to advisor-led clients, stock plan vesting events, positive recruiting trends, and self-directed clients.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says it is increasing the cash component of advisor compensation, changes that support the firm's overall investment into its financial advisors.
items.quote: we will also increase the cash component of our advisor compensation... these changes support our overall investment into our financial advisors and will help simplify our compensation program

a1.MS.reason: Multiple passages directly describe how Morgan Stanley recruits financial advisors (employee loans program, selective recruiting on an integrated platform, inbound inquiry, workplace-originated flows), so these are facts.

a2.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley recruits certain Wealth Management financial advisors through an employee loan program established primarily for that purpose; the loans are full recourse, require periodic repayments, and are due in full upon termination.
items.quote: Employee loans are granted in conjunction with a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors, are full recourse and generally require periodic repayments, and are due in full upon termination of employment with the Firm.

items.text: In Q2 2025, advisor-led asset flows were strong and originated from new advisors attracted to the strength of the workplace platform.
items.quote: Advisor-led flows were particularly strong, originating from new advisors who are attracted to the strength of the workplace, as well as assets that originated from workplace.

items.text: Advisor-led growth comes from existing advisors as well as recruits and from workplace origination.
items.quote: Advisor-led is coming both from existing advisors as well as recruits and the origination of workplace.

items.text: Morgan Stanley has recruits interested in what it has been investing in, and recruiting on the advisor-led side is complemented by flows from workplace.
items.quote: We have recruits that are interested in what we've been investing in... From the advisor-led side, we do have recruiting, but we also have flows coming in from workplace.

a2.MS.reason: Passages state MS recruits certain Wealth Management financial advisors (via an employee loan program) and that advisor-led growth comes from new advisors/recruits attracted to its platform, though they do not explicitly distinguish experienced/rookie/team/breakaway categories.

a3.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley provides recruited advisors with "recruiting bonus loans" that are repayable; the firm sought to claw back $2.46 million in such loans from a San Francisco advisor.
items.quote: turned aside Morgan Stanley's attempt to claw back $2.46 million in recruiting bonus loans, along with attorney's fees and interest

items.text: Morgan Stanley provides "recruiting bonus money" to advisors via promissory notes, described as loans that brokers pay back to firms over time; an arbitrator awarded the firm $8.13 million in damages from a former advisor over such promissory notes.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley sought to claw back recruiting bonus money from Cohen... The arbitrator ruled Cohen was liable for $8.13 million in damages to Morgan Stanley

a3.MS.reason: Trade press states Morgan Stanley offers recruited advisors 'recruiting bonus' loans/promissory notes (transition/recruiting compensation) that are repayable; the firm's own filings discuss only formulaic advisor payouts and DCP, not specific transition packages.

a4.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley sponsors deferred cash-based compensation and stock-based compensation programs for financial advisors in the Wealth Management segment that generally contain vesting, clawback and cancellation provisions; advisor deferred compensation is generally composed of 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards.
items.quote: The Firm sponsors a number of deferred cash-based compensation programs and stock-based compensation programs for current and former employees, including financial advisors in the Wealth Management business segment, which generally contain vesting, clawback and cancellation provisions. Deferred compensation for financial advisors in the Wealth Management business segment is generally composed of 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards.
items.scope: Wealth Management business segment financial advisors

items.text: Morgan Stanley's compensation programs have four key objectives including 'attract and retain top talent,' and include annual bonuses, retirement savings plans with matching contributions, an employee stock purchase plan, student loan refinancing and a financial wellbeing program.
items.quote: deliver pay for sustainable performance, attract and retain top talent, align with shareholder interests and mitigate excessive risk-taking. In addition to salaries, these programs (which vary by location) include annual bonuses, retirement savings plans with matching contributions, an employee stock purchase plan, student loan refinancing and a financial wellbeing program.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states its talent development programs are designed to provide employees resources to achieve career goals and that supporting employee development and growth contributes to long-term retention.
items.quote: Our talent development programs are designed to provide employees with the resources to help them achieve their career goals, build management skills and lead their organizations. We believe supporting employee development and growth contributes to long-term retention.

items.text: To facilitate talent attraction and retention, Morgan Stanley supports its employees with competitive compensation, benefits, and health and wellbeing programs.
items.quote: To facilitate talent attraction and retention, we strive to make Morgan Stanley a meritocratic and inclusive workplace that offers opportunities for our employees to grow and develop in their career. We support our employees with competitive compensation, benefits, and health and wellbeing programs.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is increasing the cash component of its advisor compensation, which supports its overall investment into its financial advisors and helps simplify its compensation program.
items.quote: we will also increase the cash component of our advisor compensation. We are making these changes to reduce the accounting-driven volatility in revenues and earnings... these changes support our overall investment into our financial advisors and will help simplify our compensation program.

items.text: Trade press describes Morgan Stanley's deferred compensation, which requires advisors to stay for years to vest and is forfeited if an advisor leaves, as 'golden handcuffs' used for retention.
items.quote: Giants like Morgan Stanley for years have taken a small amount of an advisor's gross revenue, called it deferred compensation, and required advisors to stay for years in order to vest. If a financial advisor leaves a firm with a deferred compensation plan, he or she forfeits that compensation, which is also known on Wall Street as golden handcuffs.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is not introducing retention bonuses as part of its 2027 pay plan for advisors and is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, adhering to a more traditional approach.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch are not introducing retention bonuses as part of their 2027 pay plans for advisors, adhering to a more traditional approach... Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors have to generate that much more revenue to see the same pay next year.

a4.MS.reason: Passages describe Morgan Stanley's compensation, deferred compensation, and development programs and pay-plan decisions used to retain financial advisors.

a5.MS.label: fact

items.text: CEO Ted Pick says advisors are coming toward Morgan Stanley's platform and that the financial advisor sees the integrated firm as offering unique access to intellectual capital, world-class technology, and compensation viewed as fair and motivating.
items.quote: the financial advisor is seeing the integrated firm for what it is, which is we can offer unique access to intellectual capital, world-class technology, compensation that is viewed to be fair and motivating, and the entire thing works.

items.text: CFO Sharon Yeshaya states there is a great platform and that recruits are interested in what Morgan Stanley has been investing in.
items.quote: There's obviously a great platform. We have recruits that are interested in what we've been investing in.

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes a market leading platform to power growth for financial advisors.
items.quote: Market Leading Platform to Power Growth for Financial Advisors

items.text: CEO Ted Pick says delivering on new relationships and net new asset growth creates opportunities for the team of world-class financial advisors to tap into the integrated firm for their clients.
items.quote: Delivering on new relationships and net new asset growth creates opportunities for our team of world-class financial advisors to tap into the integrated firm for their clients.

items.text: CFO Sharon Yeshaya says financial advisers, the culture of continued innovation, and the ability to provide unique capabilities and products are the foundation of the business, underpinning a scaled, differentiated platform.
items.quote: Our financial advisers, our culture of continued innovation, our ability to provide unique capabilities and products are the foundation of our business.

items.text: CEO Ted Pick says ongoing investments in Morgan Stanley's world-class platform, including investments to support its advisors, serve as an engine for future growth.
items.quote: Ongoing investments in our world-class platform, including investments to support our advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and the expansion of our essential workplace channel, serve as an engine for future growth.

a5.MS.reason: Passages state how Morgan Stanley pitches its advisor value proposition around its integrated platform, technology, and product capabilities; no passage describes pitching autonomy.

items.quote: Ensuring access to a steady lead flow is an important currency for recruitment, as it can accelerate growth for early- and mid-tenure solo practitioners, as well as teams that tend to be more effective at converting leads.

items.text: Research states that firms must re-evaluate their recruiting focus, moving away from attracting recruits with an 'eat what you kill' mentality toward a more service- and nurture-oriented way of working with clients.
items.quote: The industry's long-standing interest in attracting recruits with an 'eat what you kill' mentality must evolve as new advisors and the industry at large transform toward a more service and nurture-oriented way of working with clients.

a1.research.reason: The passages describe industry-level approaches to advisor recruiting (lead flow as a recruiting currency and a shift in recruiting focus).

a2.research.label: fact

items.text: Research identifies early- and mid-tenure solo practitioners and teams as the advisor groups that benefit from and are targeted through steady lead flow in recruiting.
items.quote: as it can accelerate growth for early- and mid-tenure solo practitioners, as well as teams that tend to be more effective at converting leads

items.text: Research notes that new advisors (advisors new to the business) are a recruiting focus, and that teams are particularly important for them.
items.quote: an advisor doesn't necessarily need to do both well, particularly an advisor new to the business. This is especially true when advisors work in teams

a2.research.reason: Passages identify recruiting targets at an industry level (early/mid-tenure solo practitioners, teams, and new advisors).

a3.research.label: not_found
a3.research.reason: No passage states what firms offer as transition or recruiting compensation (e.g., signing bonuses or transition packages).

a4.research.label: fact

items.text: Research states that wealth management firms are enhancing succession-planning strategies and broadening options to retain client assets, including codified transition approaches within existing advisor teams, matchmaking services for junior-senior advisor teaming, an internal marketplace for advisors to buy practices, capital to mid-career advisors to acquire practices, and increased retirement packages to prevent flight to independence.
items.quote: wealth management firms are enhancing their succession-planning strategies and broadening the options available to advisors to include codified transition approaches within existing advisor teams, matchmaking services for junior-senior advisor teaming focused on succession, development of an internal marketplace for advisors to buy practices, providing capital to mid-career advisors to acquire practices, and increasing retirement packages to prevent the flight to independence.

a4.research.reason: The passage lists firm-level retention incentives and succession programs used to retain advisors and client assets.

a5.research.label: not_found
a5.research.reason: No passage states how firms pitch their value proposition around platform, products, or autonomy; the lead flow and service team content concerns recruiting approach and workload rather than a value-proposition pitch.

a7.research.label: not_found

a8.research.label: different_quantity

items.text: Research reports that 32 percent of investors switch firms when their existing advisor leaves for retirement or other reasons, a measure of the client impact of advisor departures rather than advisor turnover itself.
items.quote: 32 percent of investors switch firms when their existing advisor leaves for retirement or other reasons, according to our survey of affluent and high-net-worth investors.
items.unit: percent of investors who switch firms when their advisor leaves

a8.research.differs_because: It measures investor/client attrition when an advisor departs, not the advisor turnover or departure rate itself.
a8.research.reason: No passage discloses advisor turnover; the 32% figure is a related but different measure (investors switching when advisors leave).

The three firms' recruiting and retention approaches can be compared qualitatively on the evidence, though no single common metric is directly comparable (advisor headcount is defined differently by each firm, net new assets attributable specifically to recruiting is not reported by any of the three, and turnover is reported on different bases). Morgan Stanley positions itself as selective, using an integrated-firm platform with intellectual capital and technology, and relies on deferred compensation as golden handcuffs for retention while not introducing retention bonuses in its 2027 pay plan. Merrill combines experienced-advisor recruiting (ramped back up after 2023) with an extensive Advisor Development Program for training new advisors, and reports attrition at near historic lows. Raymond James leads with culture and capabilities over the highest check, offers multiple affiliation options via AdvisorChoice, is disciplined on transition assistance, and cites a 97% advisor satisfaction rate and roughly 1% regretted attrition.
