a1.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab states it has built its advisor business around helping independent advisors grow, compete and succeed, through a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology, and dedicated service and support.
items.quote: We have built our adviser business around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed. Today, we serve more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets with a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology and dedicated service and support.

items.text: Schwab describes its Advisor Services segment as one of the largest providers of custodial, trading, banking, and support services to RIAs, maintaining its competitive position through sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed.
items.quote: Management believes that we can maintain our competitive position primarily through the efforts of our sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams, which are dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed in serving their clients.

items.text: Schwab describes its offering as "the leading RIA support ecosystem" that helps advisors serve their clients by providing wealth tools, investment/lending products, and technology in addition to custody and service.
items.quote: The leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, providing wealth tools, investment / lending products, & technology in addition to custody & service

items.text: Schwab's CEO describes Schwab's role as providing a platform and a support ecosystem that helps advisors support their clients and helps their firms thrive, rather than dictating what advisors should become or how big they should be.
items.quote: Our job and our role is to provide a platform and a support ecosystem that helps you support your clients and helps your firm thrive.

items.text: A Schwab spokesperson describes Schwab as focused on creating long-term value and access for advisors and retail investors, saying few firms can bring together custody, trading, banking, lending, wealth management, workplace and retail investing at Schwab's scale and value with the best client service.
items.quote: Schwab is focused on creating long-term value and access for advisors and retail investors. Few firms can bring together custody, trading, banking, lending, wealth management, workplace and retail investing at Schwab's scale and value - with the best client service, year after year.

items.text: Schwab's CEO says Schwab is increasingly trying to play the role of "being their bank" for independent advisors, helping them manage both sides of the balance sheet for their clients so they can compete with wirehouses.
items.quote: We are increasingly trying to play a role of being their bank and helping them manage both sides of the balance sheet for their clients.

items.text: Schwab's CEO describes its advisor services value proposition as winning across every dimension through size, scale, and the breadth and strength of its capabilities, including its custody offering, consulting and advice, and support for advisors' drive to independence.
items.quote: we're winning across every dimension, and I think it's hard for other firms to compete with our size, scale, and the breadth and strength of our capabilities, whether it's the custody offering... whether it's the consulting and advice and expertise that we bring, the support we bring to help them in their drive to independence.

items.text: Schwab's CEO describes the firm's value proposition to advisors as "never been stronger," citing the leading custodial offer ("the Schwabiest choice"), continued investment in the business, and newly added lending capabilities.
items.quote: In Advisor Services, we continue to have the leading custodial offer. We say it's -- we're the Schwabiest choice... our value proposition to advisers has never been stronger.

items.text: Schwab's CEO says it is deepening relationships with RIA firms by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody to add value for RIAs, including lending support, alternatives capability, and an expanded institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform.
items.quote: we're deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms we serve by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs.

a1.SCHW.reason: The passages directly describe how Schwab presents its value proposition to independent advisors, with no single numeric quantity asked for, so each descriptive statement is captured as a fact.

a2.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James describes its independent advisor value proposition as 'A partnership in independence,' where affiliating as an independent contractor gives access to the firm's full capabilities at a level right for the advisor's business.
items.quote: A partnership in independence. Standing apart doesn't mean you need to stand alone. When you affiliate with Raymond James as an independent contractor, you can access our full capabilities at a level that's right for your business.

items.text: Raymond James describes 'Powerful independence' for independent advisors: serving clients and growing an independent practice without wanting for capability, with the support of a full-service, self-clearing NYSE-member broker/dealer.
items.quote: Powerful independence. Serve your clients and grow your independent practice without wanting for capability, expert insight or client resources. Everything we have is yours when you want it. Enjoy the rewards of running your own practice with the support of a full-service, self-clearing New York Stock Exchange-member broker/dealer.

items.text: Raymond James describes its value proposition as a unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture, coupled with leading technology and solutions, together with a strong balance sheet and commitment to independence.
items.quote: We offer a unique combination of an advisor and client-focused culture, coupled with leading technology and solutions. This value proposition, coupled with our strong balance sheet and commitment to independence, is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.

items.text: Raymond James describes its value proposition as 'best of both worlds,' offering a unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, which resonates with advisors across all affiliation options.
items.quote: Our best-of-both-worlds value proposition, where we offer a unique combination of an advisor and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, continues to resonate with advisors across all of our affiliation options.

items.text: Raymond James states advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities, offering a unique combination of an adviser- and client-focused culture together with leading technologies, products and solutions.
items.quote: At Raymond James, advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities. We offer a unique combination of an adviser and client-focused culture together with leading technologies, products and solutions advisers need to serve clients at a high level.

items.text: Raymond James describes its value proposition as the scope and breadth of products and capabilities to serve complex client needs, combined with a strong culture anchored on putting people first.
items.quote: We are unique in having the scope and breadth of products and capabilities to serve complex needs of clients, combined with our strong culture that is anchored on putting people first.

items.text: Raymond James describes attracting advisors through its unique culture, leading service, and robust platform, while valuing independence so advisors can provide objective advice to clients.
items.quote: We attract and retain financial advisors with our unique culture, leading service, and robust platform, whereas many of our competitors compete with the largest check. We value independence to foster an environment where our advisors can provide objective advice to their clients.

items.text: Raymond James describes its differentiation as its culture and the way its financial professionals and advisers serve clients through trusted, personal relationships that cannot be replicated by AI or technology.
items.quote: But what sets Raymond James apart is the same thing that has always set us apart, our culture and the way our financial professionals and advisers serve clients through trusted relationships. That can't be replicated by AI or technology, but it will be helped by AI and technology.

items.text: Raymond James describes focusing on 'the Power of Personal' personal relationships with financial advisors, combined with roughly $1 billion in technology investment, as its differentiator.
items.quote: we're focused on the long term, we're focused on the Power of Personal, the personal relationships, and we're able to invest $1 billion in technology.

items.text: Raymond James attributes its ability to attract high-quality advisors to its values-based culture, commitment to service, and the unique ways it provides services to financial advisors.
items.quote: Our ability to attract high quality advisors is based on our values-based culture, our commitment to service, and the unique ways in which we provide services to our financial advisors.

items.text: Raymond James describes a stable, long-term platform where advisors have confidence their business, team and clients will have a stable platform for the long-term as what resonates most with advisors.
items.quote: Having a stable platform like Raymond James, where they have confidence that their business, their employees, their team, and most importantly, their clients will have a stable platform for the long-term, is really what resonates the most.

a2.RJF.reason: The passages contain multiple explicit statements by Raymond James describing its value proposition to advisors (including independent advisors), so these are facts.

a3.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James describes its value proposition to advisors as a "best of both worlds" proposition combining an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology and solutions.
items.quote: Our best-of-both-worlds value proposition, where we offer a unique combination of an advisor and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, continues to resonate with advisors across all of our affiliation options.

items.text: Raymond James states that advisors "do not have to choose between culture and capabilities," offering an advisor- and client-focused culture along with leading technology, products and solutions.
items.quote: advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities. We offer a unique combination of an adviser and client-focused culture along with the leading technology, products and solutions advisers need to serve clients at a high level.

items.text: For independent contractors, Raymond James promises "powerful independence" and access to full capabilities with the support of a full-service, self-clearing broker/dealer.
items.quote: Powerful independence. Serve your clients and grow your independent practice without wanting for capability, expert insight or client resources. Everything we have is yours when you want it... Enjoy the rewards of running your own practice with the support of a full-service, self-clearing New York Stock Exchange-member broker/dealer.

items.text: For independent RIAs, Raymond James offers "complete freedom and control" with the robust support of a premier financial services firm, described as "do it all your way, but never alone."
items.quote: you'll have complete freedom and control to do what's best for both, along with the robust support of a premier financial services firm... Do it all your way, but never alone.

items.text: Raymond James offers multiple affiliation options under "AdvisorChoice," letting advisors match their goals to the affiliation option offering a combination of support, freedom and flexibility.
items.quote: Through AdvisorChoice®, you have the ability to match your professional goals to the affiliation option that's right for you, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility – and all backed by the full support of a leading independent financial firm.

items.text: Raymond James states it has "the largest addressable market in the industry" because it offers all affiliation options and is "agnostic" as to how an advisor affiliates.
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market in the industry because we have all the affiliation options that an adviser could possibly want. And we have adviser choice where we're agnostic into how you affiliate with Raymond James.

items.text: Raymond James says its independent contractor options are designed to help advisors build their businesses with as much or as little support as they determine they need.
items.quote: Our independent contractor financial advisor options are designed to help our advisors build their businesses with as much or as little of our support as they determine they need.

items.text: Raymond James says it values independence to foster objective advice, and contrasts its stable long-term platform with competitors seeking an exit in three to five years or changing comp plans to cross-sell bank products.
items.quote: We value independence to foster an environment where our advisors can provide objective advice to their clients, whereas many of our competitors change their comp plans every year to cross-sell more bank products.

a3.RJF.reason: The passages contain Raymond James's own description of its value proposition to independent advisors across its affiliation options (independent contractor, RIA & Custody, AdvisorChoice), which are the facts relevant to this comparison for RJF.

Raymond James: In its 2025 10-K (fiscal period ended September 30, 2025), Raymond James attributes its ability to attract high-quality advisors to its values-based culture, commitment to service, and the unique ways it provides services to financial advisors. Raymond James: On the Q3 2025 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Raymond James describes a stable, long-term platform where advisors have confidence their business, team and clients will have a stable platform for the long-term as what resonates most with advisors. Raymond James states: 'Having a stable platform like Raymond James, where they have confidence that their business, their employees, their team, and most importantly, their clients will have a stable platform for the long-term, is really what resonates the most.'

The side-by-side comparison of the two firms' value propositions to independent advisors is valid on this evidence as a qualitative comparison, not a ranking of figures: both firms describe their value proposition in their own words, over overlapping themes but with different emphases and scopes. Schwab (a custodian to RIAs) emphasizes scale and the breadth of a custody-centered platform and support ecosystem—custody, trading, banking, lending, technology, and dedicated service—to help independent advisors grow, compete, and succeed. Raymond James (a broker/dealer offering multiple affiliation options, including independent contractor and RIA channels) emphasizes an advisor- and client-focused culture combined with capabilities and technology, framed around independence and advisor choice, describing a best-of-both-worlds proposition and attracting advisors with culture, service, and platform rather than the largest check. Because these are qualitative self-descriptions, no same-basis numeric comparison applies; the scopes also differ between Schwab's RIA custody offering and Raymond James's affiliation options.

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), management referenced ultra-high net worth clients as a distinct category, including offering family office infrastructure solutions to them: "for ultra-high net worth family office infrastructure solutions."

Morgan Stanley: In its 2025 Form 10-K (segment Wealth Management), Morgan Stanley states its U.S. Bank Subsidiaries provide loans to high to ultra-high net worth individuals, including tailored lending to ultra-high net worth clients: "accept deposits, provide loans to a variety of customers, including large corporate and institutional clients, as well as high to ultra-high net worth individuals."

Merrill: In a Bank of America investor-day presentation (published November 5, 2025), Merrill segments clients along a Wealth Continuum that divides clients into Mass Affluent ($500K to $1MM) and High Net Worth ($1MM to $10MM) tiers: "Wealth Continuum Mass Affluent ($500K - $1MM) High Net Worth ($1MM - $10MM)."
Merrill: In the 2025 Form 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025), Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business is described as serving clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets.
Merrill: In a Bank of America investor-day presentation (published November 5, 2025), Merrill counts 750,000 households with $500,000 or more in assets: "750K $500K+ households."
Merrill: In a Bank of America investor-day presentation (published November 5, 2025), Merrill counts 54,000 households with $10 million or more in assets: "54K $10MM+ households."

Merrill: On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets in 3Q26, up 17%: "Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets, up 17%."

Merrill: On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), the Private Bank added 470 net new relationships with at least $3 million under management in 3Q26: "the Private Bank added 470 net new relationships with at least $3 million under management."

Merrill: In a Bank of America deck (period ended March 31, 2026), Merrill defines its primary households as those with $250,000 or more in investable assets within the enterprise, excluding Stock Plan and Banking-only households.

Merrill: In a Bank of America press release (period ended September 30, 2026), Merrill households are defined as $250K+ in investable assets, excluding stock plan and banking-only households: "Merrill includes households with $250K+ in investible assets, excluding stock plan and banking-only households."

Merrill: In a Bank of America press release (period ended September 30, 2026), Bank of America Private Bank relationships are defined as $3MM+ in total balances: "Private Bank includes relationships with $3MM+ in total balances."

Morgan Stanley: In its 2025 Form 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025), Morgan Stanley describes its Wealth Management individual investor clients as including "high and ultra-high net worth individuals," naming two wealth tiers.

Morgan Stanley: In its 2025 Form 10-K, Morgan Stanley states that its U.S. Bank Subsidiaries provide loans to "high to ultra-high net worth individuals," using the wealth tier labels high net worth and ultra-high net worth.

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley's CEO references "ultra-high net worth family office infrastructure solutions" as an offering for its ultra-high net worth client tier.

Merrill: In a Bank of America investor-day presentation (published November 5, 2025), Merrill (via Bank of America's GWIM) frames its client segmentation as a Wealth Continuum that includes a Mass Affluent tier spanning $500K to $1MM: "Wealth Continuum Mass Affluent ($500K - $1MM)."
Merrill: In a Bank of America investor-day presentation (published November 5, 2025), the Wealth Continuum also includes a High Net Worth tier spanning $1MM to $10MM: "High Net Worth ($1MM - $10MM)."

Merrill: In the 2025 Form 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025), Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business provides a high-touch client experience through a network of financial advisors focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets.

Merrill: In the 2025 Form 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025), Bank of America Private Bank, together with Merrill Wealth Management's Private Wealth Management business, provides comprehensive wealth management solutions targeted to high net worth and ultra high net worth clients, as well as customized solutions to meet clients' wealth structuring, investment management, trust and banking needs, including specialty asset management services.

Merrill: Trade press reports (September 8, 2026) that Merrill's Private Wealth Management business serves high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients, with advisors aligned to a private wealth division/unit.

Morgan Stanley vs. Merrill: The two firms' wealth-tier segmentation schemes differ structurally and are not directly comparable on dollar breakpoints. Morgan Stanley names two wealth tiers — high and ultra-high net worth individuals — but its passages state no dollar thresholds defining them, and it segments Wealth Management clients by channel (Advisor-Led, Self-Directed, Workplace) rather than by wealth tier (2025 Form 10-K). Merrill, by contrast, publishes explicit dollar breakpoints: a Wealth Continuum dividing Mass Affluent ($500K–$1MM) and High Net Worth ($1MM–$10MM), an advisory business focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets, and Private Bank relationships defined at $3MM+ in total balances.

claims.text: On this evidence, the comparison can be made, and Merrill is the most explicit of the five: in its Wealth Continuum, Bank of America/Merrill explicitly names 'Mass Affluent' as a client segment, defined as clients with $500K to $1MM in assets, alongside 'High Net Worth' ($1MM–$10MM) (BAC-DECK-2025-investor-day#12). By contrast, Morgan Stanley names 'individual investors' and 'high and ultra-high net worth individuals' but never uses the term 'mass-affluent' (MS-10K-2025#125, MS-10K-2025#419); Schwab names 'affluent' clients and wealth tiers spanning 'new investors to ultra high net worth' rather than 'mass-affluent' (SCHW-TR-2025Q4#11, SCHW-TR-2026Q3#11, SCHW-DECK-2026Q3#23); and Edward Jones names 'individual investors,' 'High Net Worth,' and 'Next Generation investors' but not 'mass-affluent' (EDJ-10K-2025#9, EDJ-10K-2025#88). Raymond James does not name a mass-affluent segment in the documents searched. The comparison is valid for naming explicitness: Merrill explicitly names the segment, while the others name broader or different (higher-wealth or younger) categories.

Merrill: Merrill reports 750,000 households with $500K or more in assets.

Industry research: Cerulli senior director Scott Smith says that traditionally wealth management firms (the industry generally) have preferred to begin client relationships only after prospects reached addressable asset minimums of $250,000 to more than $1 million, implying the industry has historically not served the mass-affluent segment, which Cerulli defines at $100,000 to $2 million.
Merrill: Merrill and the Private Bank describe themselves as serving the wealth continuum of clients.

Merrill: Merrill's Investor Day presentation defines the mass-affluent segment within its Wealth Continuum as clients with $500,000 to $1,000,000 in assets.

Industry research: Cerulli estimates this mass-affluent segment comprises 46.9 million households controlling about $25 trillion in financial assets as of 2025.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: Jon Beatty, head of Schwab Advisor Services, stated (October 27, 2026) that 68% of affluent Americans say they're willing to pay for advice today, up from 38% in 2010, calling it 'the market opportunity.' Why it might matter: Beatty framed the rise from 38% in 2010 to 68% today as evidence of 'a bull market for advice' and called it 'the market opportunity.'

Merrill: In Q3 2026, Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets, up 17%. Why it might matter: Merrill attributes these results to strong demand for advice and its ability to attract clients and experienced advisers to the platform.

Merrill: In Q3 2026, Merrill and the Private Bank added net new $500K+ relationships across Merrill and Private Bank. Why it might matter: Merrill frames the growth as reflecting strong demand for advice and its ability to attract clients and experienced advisers to the platform.

claims.text: The Charles Schwab Corporation: Schwab's CEO states that 61% of affluent clients ages 25 to 44 prefer to consolidate their wealth and banking relationships, and that households with $1 million to $5 million in assets using only one financial services firm rose 11 percentage points year-over-year to 22% (Q2 2026). Why it might matter: Schwab's CEO frames this as evidence of a 'bull market for convenience' that is driving investors to consolidate their financial lives, and the firm expects this to grow as more investors seek one-stop shopping.

Industry research: Cerulli's March 2026 report (the most recent in the passages) reports that middle-market and mass-affluent households' wealth grew from $14 trillion in 2013 to $25 trillion in 2025, while their share of financial assets fell from 43% to 24%. Why it might matter: Cerulli says these households are becoming increasingly important for providers and advisors as their wealth grows, and notes this $25 trillion market is typically younger and less advised and seeks involved advisor relationships.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: Schwab's CEO states that about one-third of new clients are affluent, and the volume of new trader clients continues to increase (2025). Why it might matter: Schwab's CEO sums this up as the firm 'winning with investors of all ages, wealth tiers, and time horizons.'

Merrill: Merrill's Investor Day deck presents a 'Wealth Continuum' that defines 'Mass Affluent' as clients with $500K to $1MM and 'High Net Worth' as $1MM to $10MM. Why it might matter: Merrill states that the Wealth Continuum, within which the Mass Affluent segment sits, allows the firm to deliver as one company and is its engine for lasting growth.

Advisor headcount, how the definitions differ - Independent contractor advisors: not stated by Morgan Stanley, Merrill (Bank of America Corporation); no advisor count at The Charles Schwab Corporation ('Through the Advisor Services segment, Schwab has become one of the largest providers of custodial, trading, banking, and support services to RIAs and their clients', SCHW-10K-2025#23); stated by Edward Jones ('The Partnership’s financial advisors are employees or partners of the Partnership.', EDJ-10K-2025#35); counted by Raymond James Financial ('Independent contractors 5,065', RJF-10K-2025#227).

Advisor headcount, how the definitions differ - Date of the registered count: dated for Morgan Stanley (2020-12-31, 'Wealth Management representatives 15,950', MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1), Edward Jones (2025-12-31, 'At year end 20,425', EDJ-10K-2025#130), Merrill (Bank of America Corporation) (2023-12-31, 'Total wealth advisors (3) 18,916', BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2), Raymond James Financial (2025-09-30, 'Total advisors 8,943', RJF-10K-2025#227); no advisor count at The Charles Schwab Corporation.

(EDJ-10K-2025#35); business lines in the count: 'two operating and reportable segments based upon geographic location, the U.S. and Canada' (EDJ-10K-2025#145); not stated: trainees | Merrill (Bank of America Corporation): '(3) Includes advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking.' (BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2); business lines in the count: 'all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking' (BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2); not stated: independent contractor advisors, trainees | Raymond James Financial: 'Advisors in our RCS division are not included in our financial advisor metric although their client assets are included in PCG AUA.' (RJF-10K-2025#228); independent contractor advisors: 'Independent contractors 5,065' (RJF-10K-2025#227); excludes: 'Advisors in our RCS division are not included' (RJF-10K-2025#228); not stated: trainees.

Advisor headcount, how the definitions differ - Written definition: a count with no written definition at Morgan Stanley ('Wealth Management representatives 15,950', MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1), Edward Jones ('Financial advisors (actual)', EDJ-10K-2025#130); publishes no count of this metric; reports a related figure instead at The Charles Schwab Corporation ('perform investment advisory functions (including research)? 4127', SCHW-ADV1A-2026#1); stated by Merrill (Bank of America Corporation) ('Includes advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking', BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2), Raymond James Financial ('Advisors in our RCS division are not included in our financial advisor metric', RJF-10K-2025#228).

Advisor headcount, how the definitions differ - Independent contractor advisors: not stated by Morgan Stanley, Merrill (Bank of America Corporation); no advisor count at The Charles Schwab Corporation ('Through the Advisor Services segment, Schwab has become one of the largest providers of custodial, trading, banking, and support services to RIAs and their clients', SCHW-10K-2025#23); stated by Edward Jones ('The Partnership’s financial advisors are employees or partners of the Partnership.', EDJ-10K-2025#35); counted by Raymond James Financial ('Independent contractors 5,065', RJF-10K-2025#227).

Advisor headcount, how the definitions differ - Business lines in the count: counted by Morgan Stanley ('Wealth Management representatives', MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1), Edward Jones ('two operating and reportable segments based upon geographic location, the U.S. and Canada', EDJ-10K-2025#145), Merrill (Bank of America Corporation) ('all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking', BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2); no advisor count at The Charles Schwab Corporation; excluded by Raymond James Financial ('Advisors in our RCS division are not included', RJF-10K-2025#228).

Advisor headcount, how the definitions differ - Date of the registered count: dated for Morgan Stanley (2020-12-31, 'Wealth Management representatives 15,950', MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1), Edward Jones (2025-12-31, 'At year end 20,425', EDJ-10K-2025#130), Merrill (Bank of America Corporation) (2023-12-31, 'Total wealth advisors (3) 18,916', BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2), Raymond James Financial (2025-09-30, 'Total advisors 8,943', RJF-10K-2025#227); no advisor count at The Charles Schwab Corporation.

Morgan Stanley - How the firm reports and discloses advisor headcount: the figures cover different bases and are not one series: Wealth Management segment (ms_wm_advisor_led): 2019-12-31, 2020-09-30, 2020-12-31; whole firm: 2025Q1. The break is flagged, not smoothed.

Morgan Stanley - Advisor headcount: latest count found in the quarterly financial supplements: 2020-12-31 (MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1); no count found in the quarterly financial supplements read since (MS-SUPP-2025Q4, MS-SUPP-2026Q1, MS-SUPP-2026Q2, MS-SUPP-2026Q3).

Merrill (Bank of America Corporation) - Advisor headcount: latest count found in the quarterly financial supplements: 2023-12-31 (BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2); no count found in the quarterly financial supplements read since (BAC-SUPP-2025Q4, BAC-SUPP-2026Q1, BAC-SUPP-2026Q2, BAC-SUPP-2026Q3).
GWIM is not Merrill: the segment also includes Bank of America Private Bank.

a1.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes its three Wealth Management channels—financial advisors, Workplace, and E*TRADE—as each a category leader that, taken together, comprise its strategic client acquisition model.
items.quote: Our financial advisors, Workplace, and E*TRADE, each a category leader, which taken together comprise our strategic client acquisition model.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says it is focused on understanding "channel migration," whereby Workplace assets that began in Workplace move into the advisor-led channel.
items.quote: What we're more focused now is actually better understanding the channel migration... we have Workplace assets that began at some point in Workplace, and we're seeing them move into the advisor-led concept.

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes new flows generated from Workplace going into the advisor-led channel and becoming fee-based flows, with 70% of workplace-originated flows being net new assets to the firm.
items.quote: we have new flows that generate from workplace that are going into the advisor-led channel. Those are actually also becoming fee-based flows... 70% of the flows that come from workplace, that originate from workplace, is actually net new assets to the firm.
items.unit: workplace-originated flows that are net new assets

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes the workplace channel as a strong contributor to the top of the funnel, with workplace bringing relationships and assets onto the platform.
items.quote: illustrating the strength of the workplace channel as a strong contributor to the top of the funnel... Workplace brings relationships and assets onto the platform, and we are well positioned to support these new relationships.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says growth led by workplace relationships reflects a cornerstone of its client acquisition funnel.
items.quote: Growth led by workplace relationships reflects a cornerstone of our client acquisition funnel.

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes a differentiated workplace offering that continues to expand and source new relationships, alongside deep trust-based relationships between financial advisers and their clients.
items.quote: we have a differentiated workplace offering that continues to expand and source new relationships. And we have ultimately the deep trust-based relationships between the financial advisers and their clients.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says workplace brings in assets not just as net new assets but directly into fee-based flows, with people moving assets directly into advisor-led accounts.
items.quote: It's bringing in assets not just in NNA, but also directly into fee-based flows... they're also moving it directly into the advisor-led accounts. That's been a large part of the story.

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes the Integrated Firm as spanning from advice dispensed in corporate boardrooms to financial wellness programs for that company's employees.
items.quote: Across the Integrated Firm, Morgan Stanley is relevant to our clients, spanning from the advice dispensed in corporate boardrooms to our financial wellness programs for that company's employees.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says its intense focus on the value of advice generates movement through the funnel and allows it to capture opportunities for advisor-led assets.
items.quote: Our intense focus on the value of advice, which generates movement through the funnel, allows us to capture opportunities for advisor-led assets.

a1.MS.reason: Multiple passages describe the firm's strategy of using the workplace channel as the top of the client acquisition funnel, with workplace-originated assets migrating into advisor-led and fee-based relationships.

a2.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley states the workplace channel includes equity compensation solutions for companies, their executives and employees.
items.quote: The workplace channel includes equity compensation solutions for companies, their executives and employees.

items.text: Morgan Stanley defines stock plan participants as total accounts with vested and/or unvested stock plan assets in the workplace channel, with individuals in multiple plans counted in each plan.
items.quote: Stock plan participants represent total accounts with vested and/or unvested stock plan assets in the workplace channel. Individuals with accounts in multiple plans are counted as participants in each plan.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states Wealth Management supports clients through three channels—Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace—with workplace services including stock plan administration.
items.quote: Wealth Management supports clients through three channels: Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace. Wealth Management includes: ... workplace services, including stock plan administration

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes its financial advisors, Workplace, and E*TRADE channels as each a category leader that together comprise its strategic client acquisition model.
items.quote: Our financial advisors, Workplace, and E*TRADE, each a category leader, which taken together comprise our strategic client acquisition model.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says workplace assets that began in Workplace are moving into the advisor-led channel, with roughly $300 billion migrating since 2020.
items.quote: we have Workplace assets that began at some point in Workplace, and we're seeing them move into the advisor-led concept. Over the last five years or so, since 2020, we've seen $300 billion coming and initiating at some point from Workplace and moving into that advisor-led channel.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that 70% of the flows originating from the workplace channel are net new assets to the firm.
items.quote: 70% of the flows that come from workplace, that originate from workplace, is actually net new assets to the firm.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says it used to cite about $16 billion per year originating from workplace, and this year it is running ahead of those numbers.
items.quote: We used to say we had about $16 billion per year that were originating from workplace. This year, we're running ahead of those numbers.

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes the workplace channel as essential and as an engine for future growth.
items.quote: the expansion of our essential workplace channel, serve as an engine for future growth.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's CEO describes the Solium acquisition as the linchpin to workplace, and E*TRADE as filling out the funnel.
items.quote: we can make an acquisition of Solium before people understand that that is the linchpin to workplace, if we can add E*TRADE as filling out the funnel

items.text: Morgan Stanley says it has been focused on Workplace where it can partner with companies to reach employees.
items.quote: we've been really banging the drum on Workplace where we can partner with companies to reach employees.

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes workplace as the most exciting part, bringing in assets both into net new assets and directly into fee-based flows and advisor-led accounts.
items.quote: As it relates to workplace, that's probably the most exciting part. ... It's bringing in assets not just in NNA, but also directly into fee-based flows. ... they're also moving it directly into the advisor-led accounts.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says assets migrating to the advisor-led channel that originated from workplace grew by an incremental $20 billion in the quarter, adding to roughly $300 billion accumulated since 2020.
items.quote: assets migrating to the advisor-led channel that originated from the workplace channel as these relationships grow, with an incremental $20 billion this quarter, adding to the roughly $300 billion accumulated from workplace since we expanded our channel in 2020.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says workplace brings relationships and assets onto the platform, positioning the firm to support these new relationships.
items.quote: Workplace brings relationships and assets onto the platform, and we are well positioned to support these new relationships.

items.text: Morgan Stanley defines Advisor-Led Flows from Workplace and E*TRADE as assets brought into advisor-led relationships where the initial account was workplace or self-directed.
items.quote: Advisor-Led Flows from Workplace and E*TRADE represent assets brought into advisor-led relationships, where the initial account was workplace or self-directed.

a2.MS.reason: Multiple passages describe the workplace channel and its pipeline into wealth management (advisor-led).

a3.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley is investing in creating its referral models and products like LeadIQ that match individuals with advisers, with the goal of becoming their principal financial adviser.
items.quote: They're going into creating our referral models. They're going into products like LeadIQ that will allow us to match individuals with advisers. And our goal is to be their principal financial adviser.

items.text: Morgan Stanley works on a referral model to convert clients who do not yet have an advice-based relationship, which can begin as early as the financial education stage and with 401(k) assets.
items.quote: for those that might not yet have the advice-based relationship, we're working on that referral model. And that's something that can begin as early as the financial education spot, and it can also begin -- like I said, we have examples with 401(k)s and new 401(k) assets that come in

items.text: Morgan Stanley's client acquisition funnel sources adviser-led assets from Workplace and E*TRADE relationships; since 2020 it generated over $400 billion of new adviser-led assets from relationships originating in Workplace or E*TRADE, with the total exceeding $1.2 trillion.
items.quote: Since 2020, we have generated over $400 billion of new adviser-led assets from relationships that originated from either Workplace or E*TRADE. Today, inclusive of Workplace assets on our platform prior to the acquisition of E*TRADE, the total value of adviser-led assets sourced from Workplace and E*TRADE exceeds $1.2 trillion.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's partnership with Carta lets it offer advice-based services to individuals throughout their journey from private to public company, helping deepen relationships with private companies and their founders and family offices.
items.quote: What Carta now does is it's been interested in being able to offer these services not just to the individual founders or the top providers, the tops of the companies as they go from a private to a public state, but throughout their entire journey. We're offering our advice-based service to those individuals

items.text: Morgan Stanley expands its retirement capabilities and deepens engagement with plan participants to create more opportunities to build advice-based relationships over time.
items.quote: We continue to expand our retirement capabilities and deepen engagement with plan participants, creating more opportunities to build advice-based relationships over time.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's relevance to clients spans from advice in corporate boardrooms to financial wellness programs for that company's employees.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley is relevant to our clients, spanning from the advice dispensed in corporate boardrooms to our financial wellness programs for that company's employees.

items.text: Morgan Stanley Wealth Management provides workplace services, including stock plan administration, and retirement plan services as part of its three channels (Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace).
items.quote: Wealth Management supports clients through three channels: Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace. Wealth Management includes: ... workplace services, including stock plan administration; ... banking; and retirement plan services.

items.text: Morgan Stanley at Work services corporate clients with financial wellness and retirement plans, and these participants are counted among the Workplace channel participants.
items.quote: Retirement and Financial Wellness Participants represent participants of corporate clients with financial wellness and retirement plans serviced by Morgan Stanley at Work.
items.definition: Retirement and Financial Wellness Participants represent participants of corporate clients with financial wellness and retirement plans serviced by Morgan Stanley at Work.

items.text: Morgan Stanley connects the Integrated Firm to translate institutional strength into client value through its adviser-led and E*TRADE channels, with growth led by workplace relationships a cornerstone of its client acquisition funnel.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley connected the Integrated Firm to translate institutional strength into client value through our adviser-led and E*TRADE channels. ... Growth led by workplace relationships reflects a cornerstone of our client acquisition funnel.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's workplace channel brings in assets not just in net new assets but directly into fee-based flows and advisor-led accounts, as IPO-driven momentum leads people to move assets to Morgan Stanley.
items.quote: As it relates to workplace, that's probably the most exciting part. ... It's bringing in assets not just in NNA, but also directly into fee-based flows. People are, you know, we're seeing momentum as you have IPOs come to market. ... They're dropping into their self-directed accounts, yes, but they're also moving it directly into the advisor-led accounts.

a3.MS.reason: The passages describe the specific programs, offerings and services (referral models, LeadIQ, financial education, client acquisition funnel, Carta partnership, retirement capabilities, financial wellness programs, workplace/stock plan administration) Morgan Stanley uses to engage and convert participants into wealth management clients.

a4.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes LeadIQ, its AI-powered lead distribution platform, as matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with its financial advisors.
items.quote: LeadIQ, our AI-powered lead distribution platform, focusing on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with our financial advisors.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's Morgan Stanley at Work business, through its exclusive partnership with Carta, positions the firm as an early trusted advisor to private companies; employees across its workplace companies benefit from the firm's management of equity compensation plans, liquidity opportunities, and full-service advice.
items.quote: Our Morgan Stanley at Work business, with its exclusive partnership with Carta, positions us as an early trusted advisor to over 50,000 private companies... Employees across our workplace companies benefit from our management of equity compensation plans, liquidity opportunities, and our full-service advice.

items.text: Morgan Stanley advisors send 'next best actions' to their individual retail clients.
items.quote: where advisors were sending next best actions to their individual retail clients

items.text: Workplace assets that began in the workplace channel migrate into the advisor-led channel, a process the CFO calls 'channel migration'.
items.quote: what I mean by channel migration is we have Workplace assets that began at some point in Workplace, and we're seeing them move into the advisor-led concept

items.text: The firm provides advisors tools to bring in new clients.
items.quote: We're also bringing in new clients, and that's a lot of the tools that we've been giving to our advisors.

claims.text: On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), management described its three Wealth Management channels—financial advisors, Workplace, and E*TRADE—as 'each a category leader, which taken together comprise our strategic client acquisition model.'

On the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), management said the firm is now focused on understanding 'channel migration,' whereby Workplace assets that began in Workplace move into the advisor-led channel.

On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), management said new flows generated from Workplace go into the advisor-led channel and become fee-based flows, and that 70% of workplace-originated flows are net new assets to the firm (as of June 30, 2025).

On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), management described the workplace channel as a strong contributor to the top of the funnel, with workplace bringing relationships and assets onto the platform and positioning the firm to support these new relationships.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), management described a differentiated workplace offering that continues to expand and source new relationships, alongside deep trust-based relationships between financial advisers and their clients.

On the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), management described the Integrated Firm as spanning 'from the advice dispensed in corporate boardrooms to our financial wellness programs for that company's employees.'

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), management said its 'intense focus on the value of advice, which generates movement through the funnel, allows us to capture opportunities for advisor-led assets.'
The 3Q25 10-Q (period ended September 30, 2025) states 'The workplace channel includes equity compensation solutions for companies, their executives and employees.'

The 3Q25 10-Q (period ended September 30, 2025) defines stock plan participants as 'total accounts with vested and/or unvested stock plan assets in the workplace channel,' with individuals in multiple plans counted in each plan.
The 2025 10-K (February 2026) states Wealth Management supports clients through three channels—Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace—with workplace services including stock plan administration.
On the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), management said workplace assets that began in Workplace are moving into the advisor-led channel, with roughly $300 billion migrating since 2020.
On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), management said it used to cite about $16 billion per year originating from workplace, and that this year it was running ahead of those numbers.
On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), management described the workplace channel as essential and as 'an engine for future growth.'
On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), the CEO described the Solium acquisition as 'the linchpin to workplace' and E*TRADE as 'filling out the funnel.'
On the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), management said it has been focused on Workplace, where it can partner with companies to reach employees.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), management described workplace as the most exciting part, bringing in assets both into net new assets and directly into fee-based flows and advisor-led accounts.

On the 1Q25 earnings call (April 2025), management said assets migrating to the advisor-led channel that originated from workplace grew by an incremental $20 billion in the quarter, adding to roughly $300 billion accumulated since 2020.

On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), management said it is investing in creating referral models and products like LeadIQ that match individuals with advisers, with the goal of becoming their principal financial adviser.

On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), management said it works on a referral model to convert clients who do not yet have an advice-based relationship, which can begin as early as the financial education stage and with 401(k) assets.

On the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026), management said its client acquisition funnel sources adviser-led assets from Workplace and E*TRADE relationships; since 2020 it generated over $400 billion of new adviser-led assets from relationships originating in Workplace or E*TRADE, with the total exceeding $1.2 trillion.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), management said its partnership with Carta lets it offer advice-based services to individuals throughout their journey from private to public company, helping deepen relationships with private companies and their founders and family offices.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), management said it continues to expand retirement capabilities and deepen engagement with plan participants, creating more opportunities to build advice-based relationships over time.
On the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), management said Morgan Stanley's relevance to clients spans from advice in corporate boardrooms to financial wellness programs for that company's employees.

The 2025 10-K (February 2026) states Morgan Stanley Wealth Management provides workplace services, including stock plan administration, and retirement plan services as part of its three channels (Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace).

In the January 2026 strategic update deck, Morgan Stanley defines Retirement and Financial Wellness Participants as 'participants of corporate clients with financial wellness and retirement plans serviced by Morgan Stanley at Work.'

On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), management said Morgan Stanley connects the Integrated Firm to translate institutional strength into client value through its adviser-led and E*TRADE channels, with growth led by workplace relationships a cornerstone of its client acquisition funnel.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), management said the workplace channel brings in assets not just in net new assets but directly into fee-based flows and advisor-led accounts, as IPO-driven momentum leads people to move assets to Morgan Stanley.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), management said its Morgan Stanley at Work business, through its exclusive partnership with Carta, positions the firm as an early trusted advisor to over 50,000 private companies, with employees across its workplace companies benefiting from its management of equity compensation plans, liquidity opportunities, and full-service advice.
On the 1Q25 earnings call (April 2025), management said advisors were sending 'next best actions' to their individual retail clients.
On the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), management said workplace assets that began in the workplace channel migrate into the advisor-led channel, a process the CFO called 'channel migration.'
On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), management said the firm is bringing in new clients and that 'a lot of the tools that we've been giving to our advisors' are part of that.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), management said it invests to broaden capabilities for financial advisors, including alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.

As of the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), Morgan Stanley reported that over the last five years since 2020, $300 billion of assets that initiated in the Workplace channel moved into the advisor-led channel.

As of the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026), Morgan Stanley reported that since 2020 it generated over $400 billion of new advisor-led assets from relationships that originated from either Workplace or E*TRADE.

As of the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026), Morgan Stanley reported the total value of advisor-led assets sourced from Workplace and E*TRADE exceeds $1.2 trillion, roughly 20% of its current $5.8 trillion of advisor-led assets.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), Morgan Stanley reported advisor-led assets originating from Workplace and E*TRADE relationships grew to a record $99 billion for the full year, compared to historical averages of around $60 billion per year.
On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), Morgan Stanley said it previously had about $16 billion per year of flows originating from Workplace, and in 2025 it was running ahead of those numbers.

As of the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026), Morgan Stanley stated that channel migration of Workplace assets now seeking advice has helped contribute to over $1 trillion of total assets in its advisor-led strategy.

In the January 2026 strategic update deck, Morgan Stanley defines Advisor-Led Flows from Workplace and E*TRADE as assets brought into advisor-led relationships where the initial account was workplace or self-directed, averaged across 2020-2024.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), management reported LeadIQ, its AI-powered lead distribution platform, as an early AI use case (some live, some in pilot) focused on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with financial advisors. Why it might matter: the transcript places LeadIQ among the firm's AI use cases that are in pilot and showing progress, alongside the DevGen AI tool and Parable.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), management reported its expanded collaboration with Carta in private markets and announced partnerships with Zero Hash in digital assets as continued investments to deepen competitive moats and service clients. Why it might matter: the transcript attributes the continued migration of workplace assets into the advisor-led channel to these investments in the differentiated platform, framing the Carta and Zero Hash partnerships as deepening competitive moats and reinforcing leadership in the industry.

On the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), management reported its recently announced partnership with Carta puts it at the center of new client stock plan opportunities as private companies consider going public. Why it might matter: a related statement says the Carta partnership lets Morgan Stanley offer advice-based services to individuals throughout their journey from private to public company, helping deepen relationships with private companies and their founders.

On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said the workplace business has always been competitive, and Morgan Stanley differentiates by offering more capabilities, options and a greater lens of investment, beginning with corporate relationships built through the Integrated Firm.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), CEO Ted Pick said Morgan Stanley is in a singular position in the industry to see the integrated scaling of the funnel, with a differentiated workplace offering, and has built advantages to preserve its moat and make technology a differentiator in its favor.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), Sharon Yeshaya said assets originating from workplace continue to migrate into the advisor-led channel due to investments in a differentiated platform, and the firm deepens competitive moats through the expanded Carta collaboration and Zero Hash partnerships, reinforcing leadership in the industry.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), management said strategic initiatives such as the acquisition of EquityZen, the expanded partnership with Carta, and the collaboration with Zero Hash lay the foundation to widen Morgan Stanley's competitive moats.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), Sharon Yeshaya said the multiyear track record demonstrates a differentiated client acquisition funnel and its durability, and the platform's scale and product offering provide a powerful competitive advantage.
On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), Sharon Yeshaya said workplace brings relationships and assets onto the platform, and the firm's investments and capabilities set it apart.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), management said full-year net new assets of $356 billion and fee-based flows of $160 billion demonstrate industry-leading growth, and workplace and E*TRADE relationships continue to seek out advice (Wealth Management scope).

This comparison cannot be made on this evidence as a verified cross-firm or industry comparison: only Morgan Stanley appears in the matrix, and no competitor firm's positioning or figures are available to compare against. The available items are Morgan Stanley management's own qualitative self-positioning—describing a 'singular position in the industry,' a 'differentiated workplace offering,' 'industry-leading' net new asset growth, and investments to 'widen our competitive moats'—so the firm's positioning relative to competitors is reported only in its own words and cannot be independently checked.

duplicates_removed.text: On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), management said 'Growth led by workplace relationships reflects a cornerstone of our client acquisition funnel.'

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), management said workplace brings in assets not just as net new assets but directly into fee-based flows, with people moving assets directly into advisor-led accounts.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), management described its financial advisors, Workplace, and E*TRADE channels as each 'a category leader' that together comprise its strategic client acquisition model.
On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), management stated that 70% of the flows originating from the workplace channel are net new assets to the firm.
On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), management said workplace brings relationships and assets onto the platform, positioning the firm to support these new relationships.

In the January 2026 strategic update deck, Morgan Stanley defines Advisor-Led Flows from Workplace and E*TRADE as 'assets brought into advisor-led relationships, where the initial account was workplace or self-directed.'

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), management described LeadIQ, its AI-powered lead distribution platform, as 'matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with our financial advisors.'

In Q1 2025, Morgan Stanley reported an incremental $20 billion of assets migrating to the advisor-led channel that originated from the workplace channel, adding to the roughly $300 billion accumulated from workplace since 2020.
As of the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), Morgan Stanley stated that 70% of the flows that originate from Workplace are net new assets to the firm.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), management said its Morgan Stanley at Work business, with its exclusive partnership with Carta, positions the firm as an early trusted advisor to over 50,000 private companies.

items.text: Raymond James offers an affiliation-choice platform called AdvisorChoice®, which lets advisors match their professional goals to an affiliation option, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility, all backed by the firm.
items.quote: Through AdvisorChoice®, you have the ability to match your professional goals to the affiliation option that's right for you, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility

items.text: The affiliation options include Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, Corporate RIA, and RIA & Custody Services.
items.quote: Traditional Employee: Get everything you expect from working for a firm with a powerful difference – book ownership. Advisor Select: Lead your own branch... Independent Contractor: Operate as an independent financial advisor... Bank & Credit Union: Leverage national strength... Corporate RIA: Exercise true autonomy and support refined for fee-only practices

items.text: Financial advisors primarily affiliate with Raymond James directly as either employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors and broker-dealers served through the RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division.
items.quote: Financial advisors primarily affiliate with us directly as either employees or independent contractors or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors ("RIAs") and broker-dealers to which we provide services through our RIA and Custody Services ("RCS") division.

items.text: Employee financial advisors work in a traditional branch supported by local management and administrative staff, serve predominantly retail clients, and their compensation primarily includes a payout on revenues they generate, while also participating in the firm's employee benefit plans.
items.quote: Employee financial advisors work in a traditional branch supported by local management and administrative staff. They provide services predominantly to retail clients. Compensation for these financial advisors primarily includes a payout on revenues they generate and such advisors also participate in the firm's employee benefit plans.

items.text: Financial advisors who are independent contractors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and, accordingly, receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors.
items.quote: Our financial advisors who are independent contractors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and, accordingly, receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors.

items.text: Independent contractor financial advisor options are designed to help advisors build their businesses with as much or as little firm support as they determine they need; independent contractors may affiliate directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in the Financial Institutions Division.
items.quote: Our independent contractor financial advisor options are designed to help our advisors build their businesses with as much or as little of our support as they determine they need. Independent contractor financial advisors may affiliate with us directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in our Financial Institutions Division.

items.text: The Traditional Employee model offers up to 50% payout and a full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.
items.quote: Model: Traditional Employee ... Payout + Benefits: Up to 50% payout** and full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.

items.text: The Advisor Select model offers a 70-80% gross payout and a full array of competitive employee benefits offerings, as an employee affiliation option allowing advisors to lead their own branch and run its P&L.
items.quote: Model: Advisor Select ... Payout + Benefits: 70-80% gross payout** and full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.

items.text: The Independent Contractor model offers an 81% to 90% payout, with advisors leveraging the firm's third-party partnerships to create a benefits package that best fits their team.
items.quote: Model: Independent Contractor ... Payout + Benefits: 81% to 90% payout***. Leverage our third party partnerships to create a benefits package that best fits your team.

items.text: Advisor Select provides established advisors the full benefits of the employee channel with the independence to create their own branches; advisors choose a location, build out their office, and run their branch's P&L to earn a higher rate on production.
items.quote: Advisor Select® provides established advisors the full benefits of our employee channel with the independence to create their own branches... Choose a location, build out your office and run your branch's P&L to earn a higher rate on production.

items.text: As an independent contractor with Raymond James, an advisor can access the firm's full capabilities at a level suited to their business, with the support of a full-service, self-clearing NYSE-member broker/dealer, and access to investing, planning, private wealth, marketing and technology.
items.quote: When you affiliate with Raymond James as an independent contractor, you can access our full capabilities at a level that's right for your business... Enjoy the rewards of running your own practice with the support of a full-service, self-clearing New York Stock Exchange-member broker/dealer. Investing, planning, private wealth, marketing, technology – it's all there.

items.text: The employee advisor experience is enabled by advisor book ownership: the advisor owns their book of business, with no quotas and no product pushing.
items.quote: We've redefined the employee advisor experience, enabled by advisor book ownership. It's your business. Your brand. Your clients... no quotas, no product pushing.

items.text: The Corporate RIA model is for fee-only/fee-based practices, exercising true autonomy with support refined for fee-only practices under the firm's established RIA.
items.quote: Corporate RIA: Exercise true autonomy and support refined for fee-only practices under our established RIA.

a1.RJF.reason: The passages directly describe how the AdvisorChoice affiliation-choice model works, including the employee versus independent contractor options and their payout/benefit differences.

items.text: Independent advisor payouts are higher than employee payouts because independents cover their own overhead costs (real estate, health insurance, etc.); the employee side has tiered payout systems so higher production moves advisors up the payout grid.
items.quote: with the compensation and payouts to independent advisers versus employee advisers, of course, the independent payouts are higher because they cover their overhead costs, their real estate, their health insurance, et cetera ... even on the employee side, we have tiered payout systems. And so as production increases, you kind of get higher up on the payout grid as well.

items.text: The independent channel has a higher payout than the employee channel, which drives a higher mix of compensation relative to the Capital Markets business.
items.quote: Private Client Group business, with the independent channel, which has a higher payout. Some firms break that out of compensation. We include it in compensation

items.text: Employee financial advisor compensation primarily includes a payout on revenues they generate, and such advisors also participate in the firm's employee benefit plans.

items.text: Management states its strategic rationale is the "best of both worlds" value proposition - combining an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology and solutions - which resonates with advisors across all of its affiliation options.
items.quote: Our best of both worlds value proposition, where we offer a unique combination of an advisor and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, continues to resonate with advisors across all of our affiliation options.

items.text: Management states it is focused on the long term and providing a stable platform, attracts and retains advisors with its unique culture, leading service and robust platform (rather than the largest check), and values independence so advisors can provide objective advice.
items.quote: We are focused on the long-term and providing a stable platform for our advisors, bankers, and associates, whereas so many of our competitors are increasingly looking for an exit in three to five years or even less. items.text: Morgan Stanley states that within its Wealth Management business segment, asset management revenues are related to advisory services associated with fee-based assets, account service and administration, and distribution of products, and are generally based on the net asset value of the account in which a client is invested.
items.quote: Within the Wealth Management business segment, Asset management revenues are related to advisory services associated with fee-based assets, account service and administration, as well as distribution of products. These revenues are generally based on the net asset value of the account in which a client is invested.

items.text: Morgan Stanley defines fee-based client assets as the amount of client assets where the basis of payment for services is a fee calculated on those assets.
items.quote: Fee‐based client assets represent the amount of client assets where the basis of payment for services is a fee calculated on those assets.
items.definition: the amount of client assets where the basis of payment for services is a fee calculated on those assets

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that asset management revenues within the Wealth Management segment are primarily generated from separately managed, unified managed, advisor, portfolio manager, and cash management account types.
items.quote: Asset management revenues within the Wealth Management segment are primarily generated from the following types of accounts: • Separately managed... • Unified managed... • Advisor... • Portfolio manager... • Cash management...

items.text: Morgan Stanley reports that the average fee rate on total fee-based client assets was 63 basis points in 2025, 63 in 2024, and 64 in 2023.
items.quote: Total fee-based client assets        63        63        64
items.definition: Based on Asset management revenues related to advisory services associated with fee-based assets.

a2.MS.reason: The passages explicitly describe how Morgan Stanley's advisor-led model earns revenue on client assets: asset management revenues based on fee-based assets (a fee calculated on those assets) and generally on the net asset value of the account.

claims.text: Schwab: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states Schwab's largest sources of net revenues are net interest revenue, asset management and administration fees, trading revenue, and bank deposit account fees.

Schwab: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states net interest revenue is the difference between interest generated on interest-earning assets and interest paid on funding sources, and Schwab's primary funding source for interest-earning assets is uninvested client cash balances held on its balance sheet.

Schwab: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states asset management and administration fees are primarily earned from proprietary money market mutual funds, proprietary and third-party mutual funds and ETFs, and fee-based managed investing solutions.

Schwab: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states trading revenue includes commissions earned for executing trades for clients in certain individual equities, options, futures, fixed income securities, and certain third-party mutual funds and ETFs; order flow revenue; and principal transactions revenue earned primarily from actions to support client trading in fixed income securities.

Schwab: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states that by functioning as custodian Schwab earns revenue associated with underlying client assets predominantly through net interest revenue and asset management and administration fees, and does not charge the RIA or end client a custody fee.

Schwab: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states asset management and administration fees include mutual fund, ETF, and CTF service fees and fees for other asset-based financial services provided to individual and institutional clients.
Schwab: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states fees are generally based on a percentage of the daily value of assets under management and are collected on a monthly or quarterly basis.

Morgan Stanley: Within its Wealth Management business segment, the 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states asset management revenues are related to advisory services associated with fee-based assets, account service and administration, and distribution of products, and are generally based on the net asset value of the account in which a client is invested.

Morgan Stanley: In the Wealth Management segment, the 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) defines fee-based client assets as the amount of client assets where the basis of payment for services is a fee calculated on those assets.

Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states that asset management revenues within the Wealth Management segment are primarily generated from separately managed, unified managed, advisor, portfolio manager, and cash management account types.

Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states the Partnership primarily derives revenues from fees for providing investment advisory and other account services to clients, fees for assets held by clients, and commissions for the distribution of mutual fund shares and insurance products and the purchase or sale of securities.

Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) classifies asset-based fee revenue as revenue derived from fees determined by the underlying value of client assets, including advisory programs fees, service fees, and other asset-based fee revenue.

Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states advisory program fees are based on the average daily market value of client assets in the program as well as contractual rates, charged to clients monthly and collected the following month.
Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states other asset-based fee revenue consists of revenue sharing, fund adviser fees, cash solutions and Trust Co. fees.

Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states the Partnership earns revenue on clients' assets through service fees and revenue sharing received under agreements with certain mutual fund and insurance companies.

Schwab: The third-quarter 2026 earnings call (October 2026) states trader households generate approximately 2x the revenue on client assets of the retail average (and 7x the net new assets).

The comparison of revenue yield on client assets between Schwab and advisor-led models cannot be made on a same-basis on this evidence. Schwab does not report an absolute revenue yield (basis points) on total client assets; instead it reports revenue on client assets (ROCA) only as relative multiples — approximately 2x for Managed Investing Solutions and trader households and approximately 3x for Schwab Wealth Advisory versus retail households (with the 3x figure scoped to retail households with more than $500K in investable assets, excluding Trader). By contrast, Morgan Stanley reports an absolute average fee rate of 63 basis points, but that measure covers only fee-based (advisory) client assets and is based on asset management revenues related to advisory services associated with fee-based assets, not total client assets. Edward Jones, Merrill, and Raymond James do not report a comparable revenue-yield figure in the documents searched. Because the Schwab figure is a relative multiple rather than an absolute yield and the Morgan Stanley figure is limited to fee-based assets, the two are not comparable; no shared-period, same-definition yield exists on which to rank the firms.
